章:巴拉斯鲁姆[PARAGRAPH]这座精灵之城既奇异又美丽。城中最醒目的是孔雀石宫——一座苔绿色的巨大金字塔式神庙,顶端开着一道幽暗的拱门。奥斯陶里,即精灵长枪兵,时刻警惕地守卫在拱门四周,还有两名守在牢狱门外。[PARAGRAPH]城中其余建筑皆由灰石砌成,只是偶尔用石英晶体或苍白发光的菌类点缀那些雅致的楼宇。灰石之间不见接缝,看上去不像人工建造,倒像是从这潮湿的地里径自长出来的。城市如此昏暗,那一点微光反倒生出更多阴影,在人眼看来,整座城仿佛只是深浅不一的黑暗。[PARAGRAPH]城中最亮的光来自召唤之塔——一座矗立在孔雀石宫正前方的石塔。塔顶燃着一团金色的火焰,火焰的高度恰与那道拱门齐平。火中没有半点红或橙,只是一种纯粹的黄金之色,为这座城染上一丝淡淡的暖意。[PARAGRAPH]“图书馆里为客人备着几间客房,”范恩说道,显然仍在为他与沃德伦的争执而心神不宁,“来巴拉斯鲁姆的访客大多是为求学而来,所以我们把空房都留在那里。我们会给你们送吃的,你们尽可以在城中随意走动。在暗影之井里,你们是安全的。”[PARAGRAPH]他们在图书馆前停下。那是一座圆形的石砌建筑,只有一组宽阔的大门,不设窗户。馆顶是一座嵌着透明石英的穹顶,一片弥散的光晕从建筑内部透射出来。[PARAGRAPH]范恩推门前先眯起了眼,叮嘱众人都遮住眼睛。里面悬着一盏巨大的银质吊灯,灯上覆满发光的菌类,把整座图书馆浸在一片幽微的白光之中。墙上与吊灯齐高处镶着镜子,把光反射到馆内各处。透明的石英穹顶又让天光与城中的一点微光透了进来。[PARAGRAPH]范恩花了好几秒才适应馆里的光。对其余人而言,这是他们踏入暗影之井以来头一回能看得清清楚楚。这图书馆算不上明亮,却足够读书了。[PARAGRAPH]在石英穹顶与那圈镜子之下,一架架堆满书籍的书架填满了整个房间。在奥里克、基里恩和丹安看来,这是一座惊人的藏书。莱尔却没那么惊叹。[PARAGRAPH]“比起瑟罗兰的图书馆,这里可太小了,而瑟罗兰还算不上什么大的精灵城市。人们为什么要跑来这儿求学?”莱尔问。[PARAGRAPH]范恩领着他们走向紧邻馆内主厅的两间小卧室,一边回答:“这些典籍来自亡者之地。埃雷布斯上许多最重要的著作家,都在完成他们最伟大的作品之前就死了。而在这里,我们藏有那些作品——它们在阿拉温的国度里被写完,供人研读。”[PARAGRAPH]“我们能读它们吗?”奥里克问。[PARAGRAPH]范恩点点头:“下一位旅人来临,或许要等上几个月。我们只请你们在此期间去果园里干干活、帮忙打打水。除此之外,你们爱读什么就读什么。这里有间盥洗室,我再看看能不能给你们找些干净衣裳。”[PARAGRAPH]范恩走后,众人便在那两间屋子里安顿下来。基里恩执意要独占一间,硬是把三个男孩塞进了另一间。他们抱怨了一通,可洗漱完、换上范恩取来的衣裳后,还是让了步,把那间屋子给了她。范恩还归还了他们的武器,丹安拿起自己的长矛,伸手抚过矛上镶嵌的银与绿石——这是家乡的念想,握着它,他便觉得安心几分。[PARAGRAPH]奥里克在图书馆里一把大椅上坐下,身边堆着一摞书。他最感兴趣的是一部由穆卡恩——即冬之神——的一名祭司所写的史书。那祭司生活在上一个纪元,那时穆卡恩还活在埃雷布斯之上;书中也记载了穆卡恩死于凯洛林与弑神者之手的经过。[PARAGRAPH]莱尔和莉万娜都去睡了,占了男孩屋里唯一的一张床。他们终于安全了,能在柔软的床上盖着温暖的毯子睡上一夜,只觉欢喜。[PARAGRAPH]可丹安却坐立不安。他沿着书架踱步,读着那些他看得懂的语言写就的书名,但他从来就不爱读书。奥里克对他的搭话置之不理,他便去敲基里恩的门。[PARAGRAPH]“想去外面转转吗?”她开门时丹安问道。[PARAGRAPH]基里恩身着一条薄薄的灰色精灵长裙,裙边镶着深紫。她的头发才洗过,还是湿的,此刻赤着脚——尽管范恩连衣裳带凉鞋一并送来了。这是丹安头一回见她穿这般女儿家的装束,因为她平日总和他一样,穿着布里格达罗那种破旧的裤子和衬衫。他一时竟不知说什么好。[PARAGRAPH]基里恩打了他一拳:“不许笑!”[PARAGRAPH]他压根儿没想到要笑,只含糊应了一声,把目光移开。[PARAGRAPH]“行吧,我去。”基里恩说着,趿上了凉鞋。[PARAGRAPH]跟奥里克说了一声他们要出去,两人便推开图书馆的正门,走进了巴拉斯鲁姆。他们的眼睛花了好几分钟才适应城中的黑暗。适应之后,他们便信步朝牢狱那边晃了回去。[PARAGRAPH]整座城显得空空荡荡。虽有精灵在外走动,却极为稀少,而且他们行走时如此悄无声息,常常无人察觉。丹安见到的头一个居民,是一个精灵女子,正用大桶搅着一种紫黑色的液体。她生得娇小,兴许就是那个把裙子送给基里恩的女子。丹安走过时,那女子朝他甜甜一笑。[PARAGRAPH]两名奥斯陶里仍守在牢狱门外。丹安和基里恩小心翼翼地靠近,那些精灵战士驾着战车冲锋的记忆,仍萦绕在他们心头。[PARAGRAPH]“咱们去看看那道传送门,”丹安指着孔雀石宫顶端说。[PARAGRAPH]基里恩神色紧张,却还是点了点头。[PARAGRAPH]孔雀石宫的绿石与城中别处的石头不同。它由厚重的石块砌成,虽然彼此严丝合缝,所有的棱角却都被岁月磨得光滑。宫殿没有门,也看不出别的入口,只在四面各有一道长长的台阶通向顶端。丹安和基里恩往上爬时,注意到这宫殿没有任何装饰或铭文,唯有顶端那道弯曲拱门的正上方,刻着一个飞蛾的符号。[PARAGRAPH]宫顶轻易便有十来名奥斯陶里,四面台阶的半途上也各站着几名。他们看着丹安和基里恩爬上宫殿,一言不发。丹安觉得,他们守在这里,并不是为了拦阻谁进入那道拱门,而是为了防备可能从里面出来的东西。[PARAGRAPH]沃德伦也在宫顶,正与奥斯陶里们交谈,可丹安和基里恩一走近,他们便都噤了声。这宫殿是全城最高之处,唯有召唤之塔的火焰能与之相比——那火近得足以把宫顶染上一层昏黄。从这里能看见图书馆那苍白的白光,城中其余地方却都笼罩在黑暗里。[PARAGRAPH]“你们在找什么吗?”沃德伦问。[PARAGRAPH]“没有,”丹安紧张地答道,“范恩说我们可以随意逛逛这座城,它实在……很美。我们以前只见过自己的村子,从没见过这样的地方。”[PARAGRAPH]基里恩更是紧张,她不喜欢沃德伦打量他俩的那副眼神。他仿佛在盘算着什么,眼里却没有一丝暖意。他让她想起一个屠夫,正琢磨着为贝尔坦晚宴该宰鸡还是宰猪。沃德伦察觉到她的不安,笑了笑,那笑却只让他显得更加阴森。[PARAGRAPH]丹安转身要下台阶,却被沃德伦一句话拦住了。[PARAGRAPH]“你父亲就在那道拱门的另一头。”[PARAGRAPH]丹安僵住了,基里恩顿时觉得害怕起来。她一把抓住丹安的袖子,想逼他跟自己一道走下台阶,他却纹丝不动。[PARAGRAPH]“异界就在那道传送门里头吗?”丹安问,转过身去望着那道拱门。[PARAGRAPH]“是的,”沃德伦又露出那阴森的笑,“它通向阿拉温的国度,通向所有不被诸神认领的亡魂之处。”[PARAGRAPH]“非得死了才能进异界吗?”[PARAGRAPH]沃德伦笑了,那是一种空洞而沙哑的声音。基里恩扯得更急了,丹安却依旧不理她。[PARAGRAPH]“不,那正是我们所有人的来处。”沃德伦说,“许多世纪以前,我们便踏入了异界——那时穆卡恩尚未兴起,也尚未覆灭,人类诸邦也还未破碎。我们在异界中不老不死地活着。我们踏入那里时,范恩和海尔隆德还是男孩,比你还要年少,他们便一直如此,直到我们来到这里,才重新开始衰老。我担心,他们的心性怕是要永远停留在男孩之时了。”[PARAGRAPH]丹安走到拱门前。那只是一道简单的绿色拱门,上面刻着一个飞蛾符号。看不出它有何特别,也看不出穿过它会把你带往何处,仿佛穿过去便只是宫顶的另一侧。[PARAGRAPH]“你们为什么要离开异界?”丹安问。[PARAGRAPH]沃德伦耸了耸肩:“在异界里,我们无法生养孩子。而且那里的生活尽管惬意,较之寻常人生却总是黯淡了几分。异界是个安逸宁静之地,是个能做梦、能任凭世纪不知不觉溜走的地方。可那里的悲喜都太过淡薄。我们来到这里,是为了能真正地活着。”[PARAGRAPH]丹安心不在焉地点点头,极力想透过传送门那片空茫的气息看出些什么。[PARAGRAPH]“你若想过去,尽可以过去。”沃德伦说,几乎是低声耳语。[PARAGRAPH]奥斯陶里们听了,惊慌地交换了眼色,却无人开口。[PARAGRAPH]“丹安,”基里恩恳求道,“我们得回去了。咱们去找范恩谈谈,看能不能帮塔利亚从牢里出来。”[PARAGRAPH]可丹安转过头来望着她时,基里恩已经知道这是徒劳了。[PARAGRAPH]“回奥里克那儿去吧,”丹安神色黯然地说,“我一定要再见父亲一面。我会问他我们该怎么办。我也会告诉你母亲,你爱她。”[PARAGRAPH]泪水涌上了基里恩的眼眶。“不要。”她哀求着。[PARAGRAPH]可这没有用。丹安转过身,穿过了那道拱门。他一迈步进去,便消失了。一声低沉的呜咽,像两块石头相互研磨,伴着他的消失响起,召唤之塔顶端的火焰也危险地摇曳了一下。[PARAGRAPH]基里恩曾一闪念想追上去,可那道朴素的石拱纵然其貌不扬,却散发出一种古老而终结的气息,叫她心生恐惧。沃德伦把那阴森的笑转向基里恩,她便流着泪跑下了台阶。[PARAGRAPH]第 14 章:异界[PARAGRAPH]丹安似乎又回到了环绕布里格达罗的那片干黄的草原。万物之上笼着一层灰蒙蒙的雾霭,像清冷春夜里的浓雾,可空气却干燥而温暖。雾霭遮蔽了数百码开外的一切,叫丹安看不见那本可告诉他布里格达罗在哪个方向的矮山,也看不出这是不是他家园周遭的土地。[PARAGRAPH]转过身,他看见身后那道拱门。它孤零零地立在平原上,顶上刻着同样的飞蛾符号。正如在暗影之井里那样,它看上去只是一道石拱,另一头除了更多的黄草,别无他物。[PARAGRAPH]不知该往哪儿去,丹安便朝着自己走出拱门的方向迈步。他一边走,一边在灰蒙蒙的雾霭里搜寻任何认得出的东西。一切都既熟悉又陌生。[PARAGRAPH]一群肥硕的乌鸦被走近的丹安惊起,呱呱大叫着飞上了天。它们的喙和爪与其说是黄的,不如说是红的。丹安走近时,才看清它们方才在做什么。一具尸体躺在泥地里,被喙与爪撕扯得四分五裂。丹安分不清那是人尸还是大兽的尸首。它看上去已死了数周,除了骨头和干瘪的皮,所剩无几。乌鸦已把肉都啄食干净了。[PARAGRAPH]丹安匆匆赶路,清楚地感到那些乌鸦的黑眼睛正盯着他。他一走过,它们便又落回去继续用餐。[PARAGRAPH]他走了不知多久,或许是几分钟、几小时,又或许是几天。雾霭不散,透过它滤下的阳光叫丹安想起暗影之井里的光,只是这里更亮些。除了那些乌鸦,草原上再无一样活物。就连他细查地面,也找不到半点虫子的痕迹。他掘起的那一捧捧肥沃褐土里,也没有蚯蚓。[PARAGRAPH]丹安想过往回走——假如那还行得通的话。可就在这时,他瞥见雾霭中一个隐约的轮廓,一个方正得不似天然的轮廓。那是他认得的布里格达罗的形状。而且不是布里格达罗的废墟,而是那些仍旧屹立着的房屋,正如哥布林来袭之前他离开时的模样。丹安开始朝村子跑去,一路呼喊着他的父亲。[PARAGRAPH]草原上站着一个男人。起初丹安以为那可能是他父亲,可这人矮胖,远没有那么高。丹安走近了,才看见那人脸上有深深的伤疤,左眼也没了。他还留着一撮灰色的浓须,浓得他闭上嘴时,整张嘴都消失在须下。[PARAGRAPH]丹安认出这人就是沃德伦法杖里放出、袭击过奥里克的那个鬼魂——被奥里克解放的那一个。可他已不再是鬼魂了。他站在草原上,看上去和丹安一样真实。[PARAGRAPH]“要回家吗?”那人问。[PARAGRAPH]丹安停下脚步。他本急着赶到布里格达罗,穿过那些模糊的轮廓,跑过无疑仍守着村中广场的那些鸡,再见到所有人,找到他的父亲。可这人看上去极为庄重而睿智,尽管其貌粗犷,丹安却发觉自己不由得信任起他来。[PARAGRAPH]“是的,我想再见父亲一面。他在村子里吗?”丹安喘着粗气问。[PARAGRAPH]“是的,”那人点头道,“他在那儿,见到你他会很高兴。你村里大多数人都住在这里,过着安逸的日子。不过——”他见丹安露出笑容,便警告道,“你不能就这么去找他。他正在一场梦里,你若和他一同踏入梦中,便永远也出不来了。”[PARAGRAPH]丹安想起了身后的那个世界,想起基里恩和奥里克,想起暗影之井,想起前往瑟罗兰或不知何处的旅程。可没有什么比得上再见父亲一面的念头。[PARAGRAPH]“没关系,我想见他。”丹安说。[PARAGRAPH]那人纵然依丹安的回答对他有所评判,也没有表露出来。[PARAGRAPH]“他们会让你重新去练长矛。你的永生,将耗在那些你生前逃避的活计上。”那人警告道。[PARAGRAPH]丹安笑了:“我求之不得。”[PARAGRAPH]“还有一件事,”那人补充道,“在你来的那个世界里,海尔隆德会准许沃德伦对塔利亚施行塔盖姆仪式。”[PARAGRAPH]“塔盖姆仪式是什么?”丹安问。[PARAGRAPH]“那是死灵法师盘问受害者、又不必担心受骗的一种法子。他会杀了她,困住她的灵魂。仪式会逼她的灵魂如实回答他的问题。他会得到答案,她却会因此死去。”[PARAGRAPH]“是她帮高希偷走了心石吗?”[PARAGRAPH]“不,塔利亚是无辜的。”那人说。[PARAGRAPH]“你为什么要告诉我这些?”丹安问,他开始恼火起来,因为生前的种种事又被翻了出来。他在暗影之井里的时光,渐渐像是一场梦。他甚至已记不清塔利亚长什么模样,仿佛自被关进那间与她同处的牢房以来,已过了数月乃至数年。[PARAGRAPH]“你若回去,或许还能救她。”他答道。[PARAGRAPH]丹安愈发恼怒:“你怎么不自己回去救她?为什么非得是我?”[PARAGRAPH]“我已不再属于那个世界,你却还属于。”那人顿了顿,搜寻着合适的字眼,“你在……中间。”[PARAGRAPH]那人并未挡住丹安的去路。村子就在正前方,他已能看见基里恩母亲店铺的轮廓,他迫不及待地想用它旧日的模样,取代脑中那座城焦黑成灰的景象——正如这里的模样。[PARAGRAPH]可他没法继续往前了。他不能让塔利亚去死,哪怕他并不真正认识她。而且他知道,基里恩若得知他们要杀塔利亚,定会亲自去阻止,哪怕孤身一人也在所不惜。[PARAGRAPH]丹安没再多问,转过身,朝着那道拱门跑了回去。[PARAGRAPH]第十五章:归来[PARAGRAPH]范恩正回到图书馆时,基里恩泪流满面地冲了进来。她断断续续地说,丹安已经穿过了那道拱门;直到范恩握住她颤抖的双肩,答应会竭尽全力把丹安带回来,她才稍稍平静下来。可范恩的眼中却满是恐惧。[PARAGRAPH]他们全都奔向孔雀石宫,基里恩泪痕未干的脸上此刻写满了坚定。到了宫殿,他们纵身跃上台阶,一路冲到顶层。抵达时,奥里克因用力过度而头晕目眩,连莉万娜也大口喘着粗气。[PARAGRAPH]沃德伦站在拱门四周的奥斯陶里卫兵之间。[PARAGRAPH]“您好,我的王子。”沃德伦说,“出什么事了吗?”[PARAGRAPH]“那个孩子,”范恩咬牙切齿地说,“是你把他送进阿拉温的国度的吗?”[PARAGRAPH]“送他?不。”沃德伦淡淡一笑,答道,“他是自己去与父亲团聚的。恐怕是悲痛压垮了他。”[PARAGRAPH]奥里克闭上眼睛,伸展心神,试着运用塔利亚教他的本领,想透过那道拱门感知些什么。在他看来,那门后仿佛是一口无底深渊,任何坠入其中的东西都会被吞没,在渊壁间永远回荡。他感觉不到丹安,什么也感觉不到——直到一股突如其来的存在猛地朝他袭来。[PARAGRAPH]有那么一瞬,他感到有个人仿佛就站在他面前。那是个男人,一位布道者,一位将军,一位大法师,一位国王,或许甚至是一位神。他强大而邪恶。若那世界是一口深渊,他便盘踞在渊心。那男人与奥里克隔着两个世界彼此凝视,随后奥里克与他之间的联系骤然断绝。奥里克浑身发抖,跌坐在地。[PARAGRAPH]莱尔一把抓住奥里克,起初众人都以为奥斯陶里要动手了。拱门四周的每一名卫兵都齐刷刷转身,以一个流畅而致命的动作端平了长矛。连范恩也立刻反应过来,拔剑挡在孩子们身前,严阵以待。唯有沃德伦大吃一惊,笨拙地踉跄着退离拱门。[PARAGRAPH]方才拱门之内还只有空茫的虚气,此刻丹安却手持长矛立在那里。他缓缓放下了矛。[PARAGRAPH]“没事,”丹安有些不好意思地说,“是我。”[PARAGRAPH]第十六章:逃亡[PARAGRAPH]丹安的归来让沃德伦怒形于色。他搬出他们不许任何人从异界返回的律法,威胁要把他们全部抓起来;但范恩带着孩子们,飞快冲下宫殿台阶,远远避开了那些奥斯陶里。[PARAGRAPH]待他们走得够远、不会被人听见,丹安才拦住范恩。[PARAGRAPH]“海尔隆德要允许沃德伦对塔利亚施行塔盖姆仪式。”丹安说。[PARAGRAPH]范恩正要否认,却看出丹安言之凿凿。他是从死者之地带回这个消息的,范恩不打算质疑。范恩招呼孩子们跟上,朝精灵之城的中心奔去。[PARAGRAPH]海尔隆德的居所与旁人的并无二致。他不因身为城邦之主便让自己过上不一样的生活。范恩让孩子们在外等候,独自走了进去。[PARAGRAPH]海尔隆德正惬意地靠在一张深红色的椅子里。异界向来会钝化他们的情感,让人陷入一种舒适的浑噩;可海尔隆德在这里却难以掌控自己的情绪。愤怒与忧虑不断啃噬着他。坐在这张椅子上,是少数几件能让他放松下来的事之一。[PARAGRAPH]可范恩闯了进来,分明已到了要争执的地步。范恩还没开口,海尔隆德便已暗自思忖:若没有这个满脑子理想的弟弟纠缠不休,日子会好过多少。[PARAGRAPH]“你是不是给了沃德伦对塔利亚施行塔盖姆仪式的权力?”范恩问。[PARAGRAPH]海尔隆德深吸一口气,他知道这场争执迟早要来,只是没料到来得这么快。[PARAGRAPH]“是的,”海尔隆德答道,“我们已派猎手去追那个孩子们描述的女人。可她领先太多,我们八成永远也找不到她了。而且我们至今仍不知道高希最初是怎么得到心石的。倘若是塔利亚给了她,倘若她们本是同谋,那么塔利亚也许知道高希要往哪里去。这个机会我们不能放弃。”[PARAGRAPH]“你竟要仅凭她可能知情、却毫无证据表明她做过任何错事,就杀掉一个女人?”范恩问,声音陡然拔高,连门外的孩子们都听得见。[PARAGRAPH]“为了夺回心石,为了护佑我们的族人。是的,我会。”海尔隆德说着,努力保持镇定。[PARAGRAPH]范恩怒冲冲地夺门而出,回到孩子们等候的地方。[PARAGRAPH]“那我们现在怎么办?”丹安问。[PARAGRAPH]范恩摊开手掌,露出他从海尔隆德家中拿走的那把牢房钥匙。[PARAGRAPH]“你们不能留在这里。”范恩说,“我要去放走塔利亚,不能让她被我的族人杀害。但要把她带出暗影之井,不被奥斯陶里拦下,会很难,也许根本不可能。而你们既是从异界回来的,他们也不会放你们走。你们现在就该往井口的出路跑。奥斯陶里会去追塔利亚和我。至少这能把他们从你们的逃亡上引开。”[PARAGRAPH]“不。”丹安说,“我们不分开。”[PARAGRAPH]基里恩同样态度坚决,奥里克和莱尔亦是如此。眼见劝不动他们,又在白白浪费宝贵的时间,范恩便朝牢房奔去,孩子们紧随其后。[PARAGRAPH]到了牢房,他们发现仍有两名奥斯陶里守在那里。范恩从他们身旁一掠而过,带着孩子们走进牢中。[PARAGRAPH]牢里的塔利亚看到他们,显得十分意外。[PARAGRAPH]“孩子们不该来这儿,”她开口道。范恩却打断了她。[PARAGRAPH]“我们都要走。”他说,“不能再这样下去了。”[PARAGRAPH]可他把钥匙插进牢门锁孔时,却停住了。丹安完全明白他在想什么。他在权衡:要不要舍弃自己的家园、自己的亲人,去救一个他其实并不真正熟识的人的性命。他将为做正确的事而牺牲一切。这正是丹安在异界所做过的同一个抉择。[PARAGRAPH]随后他拧动钥匙,牢门开了。[PARAGRAPH]“奥里克,你能引开卫兵吗?”范恩问,一边握住塔利亚的手,领她走出牢房。[PARAGRAPH]奥里克把门推开一道缝,刚好能看见守在外面的卫兵。他环顾四周,竖起耳朵搜寻任何可当武器的东西。那道传送门倒是有,只是他害怕再度触碰门后的那个灵体。还有召唤之塔顶上的那团火。一如所有的火,它急切而蓄势待发。奥里克能感到它的饥渴,感到它对囚禁自己的金属栅栏的憎恨——他有了一个计划。[PARAGRAPH]“我们准备好了吗?”奥里克回头看着众人问。他们点头回应。[PARAGRAPH]奥里克伸展心神,感知那团火,将它朝自己牵引,意念催它跃下高塔,如一颗流星般落进牢房前的院子。他伸手触及它时,火焰危险地摇曳起来,他能感到它正被拉向自己。卫兵们察觉到火的移动,惊慌地抬头望去。[PARAGRAPH]随后,就在奥里克凝神之际,那火焰随着一记强大的意念牵引,竟凭空消失了。光亮不见了,奥里克与它之间的一切联系也随之断绝。他把这团火毁灭了。[PARAGRAPH]尽管这并非他原本的盘算,效果却奏效了。牢房外的院子暗了下来,卫兵们以为火焰熄灭是某种袭击,纷纷冲向孔雀石宫顶层。[PARAGRAPH]这已是他们所能得到的最好的调虎离山之计,于是众人全都冲出牢房,离开巴拉斯鲁姆,朝着沿井缘通往外界的那条小径奔去。[PARAGRAPH]他们拼尽全力奔跑,尽管肌肉酸痛、肺叶灼烧,早已超出体力的极限。可暗影之井太大了,他们连通往小径的半程都还没跑到,就听见战车朝他们追来的声音。[PARAGRAPH]一如之前,每辆战车由两名奥斯陶里驾驭,各由一头虚影般的雄鹿拉曳。它们轻快地掠过松软的地面。待它们越来越近,眼看众人再无可能逃脱,范恩转身喝令其余人继续奔跑。[PARAGRAPH]可他们全都停下脚步,举起了武器。[PARAGRAPH]布里格达罗遇袭时,基里恩的母亲曾硬把她推上小船。她至今仍为自己没有留下来协助抵御哥布林而愧疚。她不会再逃了——她拔出小刀,站到丹安身旁。[PARAGRAPH]塔利亚俯身探入松软的泥土。她祈祷着,向自己所信奉的世界祈求恩助。此地与井外那个自然世界如此不同,她在这儿几乎无能为力。可即便在这里,也仍残留着一丝埃雷布斯的灵息,她的祷告让锋利的石尖从泥土中戳出,横亘在他们与冲锋的战车之间。[PARAGRAPH]沃德伦与海尔隆德也随奥斯陶里同来。海尔隆德的命令清清楚楚——他们都得死,连范恩也不例外。沃德伦欣然把这道命令传达给了手下。[PARAGRAPH]战车先撞上了石尖。石尖伤不了那些幽灵般的雄鹿,战车却剧烈地颠簸起来,一名奥斯陶里从车尾跌落,重重摔在地上。但随即它们便冲了过来,直扑范恩、塔利亚和孩子们。[PARAGRAPH]范恩首当其冲,一杆当作骑枪使的长矛刺来。他单薄的锁子甲卸去了大半力道,却也把范恩掀得旋转着甩离了众人。塔利亚冲向他,躲过又一杆擦身冲过的长矛。[PARAGRAPH]丹安端平长矛准备迎击冲锋,可战车逼近时,他发现那长矛比自己的矛更长。奥斯陶里瞄得极准,矛尖正中丹安左肩之下,几乎将他的肩膀撕裂,只剩几缕血肉筋腱勉强连着他的手臂。[PARAGRAPH]基里恩惊恐地尖叫,她离丹安近得溅了一身他的血,但战车飞驰而过时并未攻击她。[PARAGRAPH]莱尔从另一杆长矛下钻过,纵身跃上战车后部,举匕首朝驭手刺去。可另一名奥斯陶里抓住他的胳膊,把莱尔整个提起,轻轻松松将他抛出车外;他摔在地上,无力地翻滚。莉万娜护在他身上,愤怒地朝周遭那些她无从阻止的乱斗吠叫。[PARAGRAPH]战车绕起圈来,准备下一轮冲锋。范恩和莱尔缓缓爬起。基里恩惊恐万状地俯身守着丹安。尽管奥里克看不真切丹安的模样,却知道那一击是致命的——丹安的血正汩汩淌在地上,基里恩尖声哭喊,求这一切停下来。[PARAGRAPH]这时塔利亚一把抓住奥里克,逼他直视自己的双眼。[PARAGRAPH]“你能引来某种力量救我们。来自这世界之外的东西——那道屏障并非坚不可破。伸出你的心神,把它找出来。”[PARAGRAPH]这不是请求,她并非在哀求,这是命令。战车绕圈并开始下一轮冲锋之际,奥里克伸展心神。他能感到头顶那层灰蒙蒙的雾霭,可雾外之物却少得可怜。他感觉不到塔尔奇之塔那躁动不定的能量。奥里克极力伸展,搜寻着任何东西。[PARAGRAPH]那里没有任何躁动之物,没有任何他通常会与力量联系在一起的东西,却有一股恒定而温暖的力,那是他直到来到此地才意识到其存在的东西。那是一种脉动,因为他一生都浸润其中,反倒从未察觉它竟是一样东西。奥里克伸出心神,把它朝自己牵引。[PARAGRAPH]它比他从前触及过的任何东西都更庞大,为了引导它的力量,他不得不忘却其余的一切。他的恐惧消融了,他的欲念被抛诸脑后,记忆也随着那股洪流般灌注全身的力量渐渐消失。头顶那构成暗影之井穹顶的灰雾翻腾滚涌,如同暴风雨中的海洋。奥斯陶里在眼前发生的一切面前惊惶困惑地顿住。连全无魔法禀赋的人也能感到空气中的力量——感到这世界与埃雷布斯之间的屏障正被撕裂。随后屏障崩裂,纯净、洁白的阳光倾泻而下。[PARAGRAPH]这些昔日的精灵被刺得睁不开眼,他们已有数百年不曾沐浴阳光,而此刻的光又如此耀眼,连孩子们都为之目眩。那些幽灵般的雄鹿消失了——它们的魔法只在暗影之井中生效,而那道边界已被摧毁。[PARAGRAPH]昔日的精灵中,唯有范恩没有失明。在阳光之中,他看见一个身影站立着,躯体流溢着灿灿金光。范恩知道这是一位神——太阳之神卢古斯,范恩双膝跪地,俯首膜拜。[PARAGRAPH]“因为你视真理高于一切,因为你迷失于黑暗时仍显露智慧,因为你把这些看得比自己的性命更重,我召唤了你。你将向世人重申你早已具备的那些美德。”[PARAGRAPH]范恩凝望着光晕中的神。他感到自己所有的疑虑与恐惧尽数消散。随后,卢古斯消失了。[PARAGRAPH]范恩环顾四周,一时不知身在何处。在那纯粹的喜悦过后,他不得不提醒自己身在何地。没了雄鹿,战车把车上的骑者掀翻在地,他们眼盲而茫然地躺着,沃德伦和海尔隆德也在其中。基里恩伏在丹安身上哭泣,塔利亚正试着扶奥里克站起来,莱尔和莉万娜朝基里恩跑去。[PARAGRAPH]“快走,快跑!”范恩朝小径的方向指着大喊。随后,当他注意到莱尔没理会他、径直朝基里恩跑去时,范恩又补了一句:“我去带她。”[PARAGRAPH]范恩跑向基里恩,抓住她,想把她从跪着的地上拉起。可当他看清她所蜷抱着的那具身体时,他停住了。血浸透了地面,浸透了基里恩灰色的精灵长裙,丹安双目紧闭。他已经死了。[PARAGRAPH]范恩深吸一口气,低声道:“基里恩,你得放他走了。”[PARAGRAPH]基里恩不肯松手,可当范恩把她拉开时,她转身反倒紧紧攀住了范恩,把脸埋进他的肩头,泪水化作破碎、颤抖的喘息。[PARAGRAPH]于是范恩抱起她,追着其他人奔跑。塔利亚和奥里克、莱尔和莉万娜跑在前头。女巫、银狗、两个精灵和两个孩子,一同逃离了暗影之井。[PARAGRAPH]尾声[PARAGRAPH]丹安站着,望着他的朋友们奔逃而去。他知道他们会平安无事,范恩和塔利亚会毫无波折地把他们带到瑟罗兰。连那些昔日的精灵也都无恙。混战中无人丧命,尽管大多数人都因那场袭击而青肿酸痛,还得过上几天视力才能恢复如常。[PARAGRAPH]头顶,阳光仍不断倾泻进暗影之井。地面呈现出丰润的褐色,菌类是灰白的。覆在菌类上的那些紫绿相间的游丝,在光下更显美丽。[PARAGRAPH]尽管丹安多想去追赶他的朋友们,他却能感到通往异界的传送门在召唤自己。那感觉就像他站在一汪正被抽干的水池里,一股恒定而轻柔的力不断把他拉回井心。丹安没有抗拒,转身朝孔雀石宫走去。[PARAGRAPH]离得越近,丹安走得越快。他的步行渐成缓慢的小跑,继而他飞奔上孔雀石宫的台阶,越过守卫的奥斯陶里。[PARAGRAPH]穿过拱门,丹安再度置身于那片朦胧昏黄的草原,他跑得更快,发觉自己的双腿从不疲倦,肺叶也从不灼烧。他可以永远地跑下去。[PARAGRAPH]倘若他身后有乌鸦、甚或有一道拱门,丹安都未曾留意。他确实看见了那个警告他塔利亚会死的老人。可这一次老人没有试图拦他,只是在丹安跑过时挥挥手,微笑相送。[PARAGRAPH]村庄朦胧的轮廓变成了一座真实的村庄。那些鸡与丹安记忆中的一模一样,丹安飞奔而过时,它们恼火地扑腾着散开,冲他愤愤地咯咯直叫。他终于在村中的空地上停下了脚步。加隆·艾尔正试着教卡斯宾只用双脚驾驭坐骑。这堂课上得并不顺利,卡斯宾连人带马冲过来时,两人都朝丹安大喊当心。[PARAGRAPH]基里恩的母亲正打扫着自家店铺的前廊,温和地朝丹安微笑。有那么一瞬,他记起曾在村中空地上见到她焦黑残破的尸身。可那记忆随即消融,唯一留存下来的,只有此地此刻她这般模样的记忆。[PARAGRAPH]“我父亲在哪儿?”丹安问。[PARAGRAPH]“我想他在码头吧,”她不太确定地答道。[PARAGRAPH]丹安穿过村庄,同每个人打着招呼,任由过去这几天的记忆渐渐飘散。连那之前的时光也变得模糊,仿佛此地、此刻,才是唯一真正存在的一切。[PARAGRAPH]他看见了父亲,正坐在码头尽头,身旁是一个黑色卷发的女人。她比丹安的父亲年轻,美丽动人,可丹安并不认得她。[PARAGRAPH]“爸。”丹安说,可这个字却哽在了喉咙里。[PARAGRAPH]他父亲转过身来。丹安好怕父亲会与记忆中不同,怕他会发怒,会受伤,会不再是他自己。可他与丹安记忆里分毫不差,一个微笑,便驱散了丹安所有的担忧。[PARAGRAPH]那女人也转过身,当她微笑时,眼中沁出了细小的泪珠。[PARAGRAPH]“我的孩子。”她说着站起身,把丹安拥入怀中。

[TAB]There are tens of thousands of changelings living in Esus's hell, which can appear in any form and read their victim's minds to perfectly mimic the voice and mannerisms of those they copy. There they recreate any community or place that Esus desires to deceive those trying to escape hell into forfeiting hope and returning. Unlike most of the hell's denizens, Changelings are alive, not demons. [PARAGRAPH]Occasionally Changelings are sent into the mortal world of Erebus to perform tasks for Esus. They often sire children (most commonly by replacing a lover) with mortal women. Though it is rare that half-changelings will gain their father's shape shifting ability, they are often wildly erratic, hurtful and disloyal. They are quick to sacrifice those who may care about them for their self-interest or even amusement.

The orthodox opinion of every religion or mage guild in Erebus holds that only rare individuals are blessed (or, in some cases, cursed) with affinity for any sort of magic. It is sacrilige to suggest that every mortal soul shares a natural gift in every precept, but this heresy happens to be true. While most men's affinities are too weak to be of much use, there are ways to awaken them. The architects of the Tower of Mastery go to great lengths to talk around this point rather than state it directly, but their ambition is let every mage match the powers of Kylorin.

[ICON_BULLET]Affinity lets a Mage cast more powerful versions of the spells within his sphere than will ever be available to those without this gift. This heretical offshoot of the Laeran Cord still claims to revere Oghma, but in fact they serve the angels of Ceridwen. Their Conjurers are known for causing trouble with their rituals and lack of caution.
Conjurers are like Mages that can be trained directly with no level prerequisites, but they cannot build mana nodes and are a lot more likely to miscast their spells

Gallowblight is a very deadly and contagious disease that kills most of its victims over a few horrible weeks. But those that survive are forever immune to it and are actually healthier for having gone through it.
This foul curse damns its victims to return as Undead when they die.

Elven Pox is a disease that makes the victim magically inert, keeping them from being able to use magic. It is spread by magical contact, so a mind made attempting to read the mind of a victim would contract the pox and lose the ability to use magic. This has the side effect of making the victim mostly magic immune since the pox will kill all magic that touches them.
%s1 has contracted Elven Pox from trying to use magic on %s2

[ICON_BULLET]Curse of Camulos creates an overwhelming berserker rage in the victim, often leading them into attacking others, which spread the disease. It is spread through shared pain. The rage grows as the victim causes pain. The only way to recover is to go a long period of time without causing pain or violence of any sort.

[ICON_BULLET]This disease is rarely lethal on its own, but it causes permanent rot in its victims and leaves them too weak to defend themselves. It is highly contagious, spreading through any contact with infected blood or saliva. It can quickly overtake an entire village if even one guard contracts it in combat. Certain breeds of wolves and trolls have adapted to being carriers of the disease, attacking once to infect a victims and then returning to finish off a whole settlement.

[ICON_BULLET]Cannot fall in an [LINK=SPELL_ARENA_BATTLE]Arena battle[\LINK][NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Being an Aspect of War is the highest blessing Camulos can grant, but he does not care who gets it so long as they use their power to kill. It is given at birth and cannot be revoked. All the Aspects have superhuman martial prowess, both in personal strength and in tactics. While they may not defeat whole armies on their own, in single combat are nearly invincible. Some are Good, some are Evil, and some are hostile towards both extremes, but they cannot remain neutral in any conflict for long. They are the cause of most wars, regardless of their intent. Notable Aspects of War include Arak the Erkling, Capria, Mahon the Butcher, Orthus, Magnadine, Surder, and Makhai. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Every god created seven Aspects, True Angels whose inherent affinity is exceeded only by that of the archangels or the gods themselves, and whose freedom to act in creation is not limited by The Compact. The original Aspects of War were vanquished early int he Godswar, but whenever one falls it is reincarnated as a mortal. Years can pass before an Aspect of War is reborn, but there are usually 5 to 7 active in the world at any time. The Sons of Discord try to track them individuals down and use them to cause more conflict.
[ICON_BULLET]A Spellstaff lets a unit cast twice per turn, can be broken to allow the caster to regain the ability to cast yet again

[TAB]Among the Orcs mad men are gathering, singing songs they hope will wake sleeping Dragons. They tell tales of the Flame Lord, a great Torch Dragon whose spirit has been restless since his mistress fell and who seeks an entry into our world to regain his ancient form and take vengeance on whomever he can blame for his pain.

[TAB]Acheron the Torch Dragon has made his lair in the barbarian city of %s1. [PARAGRAPH]The rage of the Orcs has summoned him from a realm of myths beyond the ether, where Bhall imprisoned the spirit of the Flame Lord once Godswar ended, back into the physical world. [PARAGRAPH]Madmen have begun to worship this beast, and others like him whom they hope to Stir from Slumber, in place of the gods. The priests of all religions warn that this Cult of the Dragon may soon become a scourge upon our land. [PARAGRAPH]Rumor has it that Acheron rests upon a bed of unrivaled riches. Multitudes covet The Dragon's Hoard, and hundreds have lost their lives seeking it. This is all in vain. Unlike most dragon species, Torch Dragons don't collect anything. The most valuable thing found in their lairs is their unquenchable mucus, which burns for days with enough heat to consume metal, stone, and even incorporeal spirits.

Completing this ritual will cool the world, changing some of the [LINK=literal]Desert[\LINK]s to [LINK=literal]Plain[\LINK]s, some [LINK=literal]Plain[\LINK]s and [LINK=literal]Grassland[\LINK]s to [LINK=literal]Tundra[\LINK]s, some [LINK=literal]Tundra[\LINK]s to [LINK=literal]Snow[\LINK]s tiles, and some [LINK=literal]Raw Mana[\LINK] to [LINK=literal]Ice Mana[\LINK]. It will also spawn occasional [LINK=literal]Blizzard[\LINK]s around the map.

This ritual gives the Immortal promotion to all of the living units the caster currently owns. Try to time its creation with a time when you have a lot of units available to take advantage of the effect. The Immortal promotion only resurrects a unit once, so this doesn't grant an eternal supply of units, but it gives every unit a second chance.

Recruits 6 Hill Giants to the player's cause.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]Early explorers found it was best to avoid the massive giants that roamed the land. A bard, named Antonis of Oriel, wandered too close and was captured by a group called the Nilhorn. He offered the only gift he could for his life, he played a song. The wild giants were so entranced by his song that, when it ended, they sat unmoving and Antonis could have simply walked out of the makeshift camp they had dragged him back to. Fascinated by finding his new audience so appreciative, Antonis continued to play, and his performances became a part of the giants' nightly rituals.[PARAGRAPH:1]Antonis stayed with the Nilhorn for three years, until one of them reported seeing a Sheaim army approaching his homeland. The giants avoided any settled land and tried to convince Antonis not to return, but he left the giants and returned to defend Oriel. Although a talented musician, Antonis was an incompetent warrior and he was killed defending Oriel. When he fell, the Nilhorn came out of the forests and approached the besieged village. Both armies froze, unaccustomed to seeing giants willing to enter civilized lands. Searching the battlefield, the giants found Antonis's body, and, enraged, they set upon the Sheaim. The village defenders cheered at their new-found allies and joined in the assault.[PARAGRAPH:1]The battle was quick and the Sheaim were turned back. After it was over, the giants picked up the body of Antonis and carried it with them into the forests. The village raised a monument to their large rescuers and swore never to forget the aid they were given. The Sheaim never forgot the failed battle either, and forever avoided Oriel in their attacks.
Six allied Hill Giants will appear in the building civilization's city.

(If previously defeated, they will be revived. ) Grants them [LINK=UNIT_ANAGANTIOS]their[\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_DUMANNIOS]respective[\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_RIUROS]avatars[\LINK] leading armies of their own. (Note: the loss of any leader's avatar removes that leader's traits. )[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET][LINK=UNIT_AURIC]Auric's avatar[\LINK] has affinity for whatever mana source may be present on his tile. The [LINK=BONUS_MANA_ICE]Ice mana[\LINK] from [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_LETUM_FRIGUS]Letum Frigus[\LINK] will remain in New Mulyr and let him cast powerful Ice spells from within that city, but he will be less powerful if he wanders elsewhere on the map. Auric must be kept alive (or resurrected) if there is to be any hope of ascending to [LINK=UNIT_AURIC_ASCENDED]godhood[\LINK] through [LINK=PROJECT_THE_DRAW]The Draw[\LINK] and [LINK=PROJECT_ASCENSION]Ascension[\LINK] rituals.

Completing this ritual halves all your cities' populations, damages all your units and causes you to declare war on every player in the game. You will also be unable to enter diplomacy with any player you are at war with for the rest of the game. It starts [LINK=UNIT_AURIC]Auric Ulvin[\LINK] on the path to godhood that will be completed by the Ascension ritual, for which this is a prerequisite. Auric the leader gains the [LINK=TRAIT_INSANE]Insane trait[\LINK]. Auric the unit gains the [LINK=PROMOTION_IMMORTAL]Immortal[\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_CHANNELING4]Channeling IV[\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_CRAZED]Crazed[\LINK], and [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_ICE]Ice Affinity[\LINK] promotions (whereever he goes, not only when there is Ice mana on his tile). There have always been men that ran toward danger. In the age of Magic, some were known as the Brotherhood of Wardens. They were a secret organization that tried to protect the citizens of Patria from cruel edicts of the Imprimator Council. They rescued elven captives from the Duchy of Dust, chattel slaves from Candlefast, and debtors from the Duchy of Glimmerhome. [PARAGRAPH]The organization started as a secular one, but the archangel Pelian the Suffering was inspired by the brave members of the brotherhood. When the rebellions began and the war started between the Empyrean, the Sanctus Inquisition and the Imprimatur Council, the Brotherhood attempted to make sure that the weak and innocent weren't destroyed in that war. [PARAGRAPH]They had middling success. Many were lost. But if they could get those they rescued back to the Duchy of Logos, they would find the tides would turn in their favor. Enemies spells were weakened, rotting wolves would lose their scent, their own endurance, and hope returned. This was the arda of Sirona and the blessing she offered for their cause. "[PARAGRAPH:2]The Brotherhood of Wardens is a cult of Sirona that teaches men that they must do whatever they can to protect the least among them. The orthodox Wardens were exterminated in Calabim lands, but Alexis encourages the spread of a heretical sect that believes the best way to protect the meek is to teach them to passively accept any form of oppression without every trying to fight back. [PARAGRAPH:2]Pelian disobeyed Sirona during the Godswar. Sirona commanded that compassion required the defense of creation, but Pelian refused to be violent and abandoned her army. After suffering a massive defeat Sirona lay nearly destroyed. As the army of Aeron closed in, Pelian returned and placed a sanctuary around Sirona. Pelian was attacked, but he still refused to fight. Instead he was torn and tortured for 21 days and bore the worst of Aeron's torments. His body is forever broken from this ordeal. But after 21 days Sirona was revived and came out of the sanctuary to rescue her archangel and scatter the army of Aeron. The breaking of the compassionate Pelian was an example to the gods that the compact was needed. [PARAGRAPH]Pelian lay recovering for centuries. It wasn't until the Age of Ice that he gazed again into creation, drawn by the calls of those suffering. There was little he could directly do, but he whispered to the great Eurabatres, who was sleeping nearby and awoke the dragon, calling him to aid those in need. [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Rebirth he attempted to calm the heart of Basium, before he marched through into hell. Pelian warned that his hubris would lead him into serving Agares, or at least remove his blessed protection from creation. But Basium ignored him and marched through the Throne of Hell. Pelian wept for him and those doomed to be lost with him. [PARAGRAPH]During the Age of Invention, when the Matronae came for the worshipers of the old gods, Pelian's spirit was with the few remaining worshipers of Sirona and called for them to be non-violent. He called for calm as they stood before the Shrine of Sirona, as their statues were torn down, as their holy texts were burned and as each worshiper of Sirona that refused to forsake their goddess was executed. Then he gathered their souls and carried them to the Isle of Birds. The Stewards of Inequity are a cult to Mammon, although few of their members will ever realize this. Mammon prefers his follows believe that they serve only their own self interest. The Stewards hate any sort of honest work but will go to great lengths to amass fortunes. Most are already very wealthy and powerful men when they join this cult, although some are merely covetous and believe membership will help further their ambitions. Its ranks include many tax collectors, regulators, government lobbyists, almost every central banker, the upper management in most large companies, and even many priests high in the hierarchies of other faiths. Few Stewards rank high enough to ever learn of the existence of the cabal that convenes to decide the policies they all execute. Most are just happy to play their small part towards the lofty goal of making the rick richer and the poor poorer. The Anointed are a cult of psychopaths devoted to Aeron, the God of Body, Strength, Sadism, Lust, Rage, Hate, and especially premeditated Murder. All of its members enjoy violence, and view killing or mutilating the innocent as a most sacred act. Although Aeron is the patron of Berserkers, he prefers the more subtle arts of the most cold hearted assassins. The cult is dominated by small group of powerful warriors called The Occisors. There is not much structure in this religion, although its members are encouraged to attain elite positions in other evil organizations. Aeron is best known as the Lord of Murder. His worshipers are usually terrifyingly powerful warriors, who could easily win most fair fights but pride themselves in never fighting fair. They prefer to strike the killing blows before their targets realize they are enemies. Aeron is also known as Maiden Friend; he has a great weakness for physical beauty, which his worshipers often inherit. They are often unwilling to harm those of great beauty. [PARAGRAPH:2]State religion allows access to:[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_DANAG]Danag the Faithful[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_SIR_HALEWYN]Sir Halewyn[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_LUIDAG]Luidag the Rag[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]Halves the production cost of: [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_HUNTING_LODGE]Hunting Lodges[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_GOVERNORS_MANOR]Governor's Manors[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_DUNGEON]Dungeons[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PILLAR_OF_CHAINS]The Pillar of Chains[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_SCHOOL_OF_SADISM]The School of Sadism[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PALACE_CALABIM]The Calabim Palace[\LINK][PARAGRAPH:2]Units of this faith are more likely to gain affinity for [LINK=BONUS_MANA_BODY]Body[\LINK] mana.[PARAGRAPH:3]The Candy Shop[PARAGRAPH:2]Sunlight filtered through the temple's stained-glass windows and cast images of angels and saints on the western wall. Within the temple parishioners shuffled uncomfortably in their pews as the Literal droned on with his sermon. The service was nearly over, and the children were even more restless than the adults. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie sat between her father and her younger brother, Artan. She was nine years old and like most of the children in the temple, was daydreaming about the many treats of the candy shop that sat in the temple's shadow. While others prayed she imagined pine nuts dipped in honey and sugar, gingerbread men and fingers sticky with pecan brittle. [PARAGRAPH]But they would only visit the candy shop if they were good during the service. It was this promise that kept the children quiet and still on Sunday mornings. It was as much a part of the children's religious experience as the Literals welcoming invocation or the brilliant arches of light that crossed the temple's dusty lofts. [PARAGRAPH]Artan swung his feet beneath the pew, risking kicking either the pew in front of him or the bottom of his seat. Amelie squeezed his hand and gave him a threatening look. Around the temple many mothers gave similar looks to their children, and Amelie's was as practiced and effective as any of them. [PARAGRAPH]The sermon closed with a final adulation and the worshipers rose to make their way out of the temple. Amelie grabbed her father's hand and Artan followed quickly behind. Now allowed to talk he was full of questions, most concerning the candy shop. They had been good so yes, they would visit the shop on the way home. And they would be able to pick one, and only one, piece of candy. It was the same as every other week, but Artan and a half-dozen other children still asked their parents if they could go, and still pleaded for more than one piece, though no parent relented. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie remained quiet. She already knew her father's answers and she was trying to pick the candy she wanted from her memory of the candy shops selection. She dreamed of caramelized pears, chewy toffee, or raisins coated with sugar and cinnamon. She carefully imagined each candy as they walked down the hill from the temple to the small shop, and changed her mind at least a dozen times. This was her favorite part of the week. Her father was sober and kind and the three of them were, for a little while, a happy family. [PARAGRAPH]The candy shop was brightly painted with a red roof and white trim over a deep green building. The front door was white, and stood beside a large window which let those on the street glimpse shelves of glass jars filled with brightly wrapped treats. The warm shop was a welcome escape from the chill wind that threatened to bring the winter's first snowfall. [PARAGRAPH]"Remember Artan, don't touch anything. " his father warned, "Pick the piece you want and tell me, so I can ask merchant Hamish to get it for us. "[PARAGRAPH]"Yes papa. " Artan answered. [PARAGRAPH]The shop's front room smelled like gingerbread and vanilla. Other families were already picking out their treats and every child carefully considered their selection, they were stuck between the desire to try a piece of candy and the fear that if they didn't look hard enough they may overlook something new and wonderful. Amelie had a different reason to spend more time picking, she didn't want this brief time in the candy shop to end. [PARAGRAPH]Merchant Hamish wandered over to Amelie as she looked at butterscotch candies in bright wrappers. He was a small man, thin and frenetic, with a weak leg that required him to use a cane. But his boundless energy made up for his clumsy three-legged gait and he made sure everyone in the shop was taken care of. He never forgot an order, and was quick to scoop, cut or measure whatever a customer requested. He wore a red and white apron that matched the color of his shop and had a crazy shock of white hair that would look unusual on anyone else, but somehow fit the shopkeepers wide, smiling face perfectly. [PARAGRAPH]"I have some ginger bread cookies I just took out of the oven. I believe you picked one last week, and nibbled on it like a mouse as you left my shop. " Hamish said. [PARAGRAPH]"I wanted it to last longer. " Amelie explained, "What are the cookies shaped like today?"[PARAGRAPH]"There were some complaints about last week's cookies. Apparently, speaker Ides didn't appreciate having his rotund figure memorialized as a cookie. And I don't know if I can afford to keep making cookies that large. So, I switched to smaller things, like buildings in the city. There are some of the cathedral bell towers, some shaped like the temple belfry, the bridge tower, the lighthouse, and the east gate. And of course. . . " Hamish added after a pause, "maybe a few fat speaker Ides hidden in the back. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie smiled, but before she could reply another family was ready to buy and merchant Hamish was off to help them. [PARAGRAPH]Artan already had his treat, an unnaturally red candied apple. He always picked the largest treat he could find, and today was no different. He sat beside his father on a low bench in front of the window greedily devouring it. Amelie's father gave her a look that meant she had to hurry up. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie finally picked a piece of swirled vanilla and butterscotch. It was so soft she could shape it with her hands and it melted in her mouth. She made tiny bites out of the thumb sized candy as her father paid for it and they left the shop for the short walk home. [PARAGRAPH]Throughout the day Amelie continued to take tiny bites from her candy, and lied to her brother when he asked if there was any left. He finished his apple before they were out of the candy shop. By nighttime Amelie had the last bite saved in the wrapper as a treat for morning and she curled up in her blankets to sleep. [PARAGRAPH]In that grey world between sleep and wakefulness Amelie imagined a bright light in her room. She opened her eyes, but the room was dark. Her tiny bed barely fit in her room, and there was no window. The only light was from her father's room, where a lamp burned. Her door was cracked, and a sliver of pale light bled into her room from the hall. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie closed her eyes and tried to drift back to sleep. When she was again in that strange limbo before sleep the light returned. This time when she opened her eyes, the light remained. [PARAGRAPH]An angel floated above her bed. Tall and beautiful he had skin like honey and light radiated out of him as if the sun set beneath his skin. As wondrous as he appeared his face was lined with concern, and his eyes were unnaturally dark. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie pulled her blankets up above her head and curled beneath them. The angel's light shone through the thin blankets and even completely covered, Amelie could clearly see her trembling hands. But the light was mild compared to the other indications of the angel's presence. A feeling of peace and warmth radiated through the room. And though Amelie had never imagined meeting an angel before, her fear melted away. She lowered the blanket enough to see the angel's face. [PARAGRAPH]"I am truly sorry. " the angel said. His voice conveyed deep compassion and though it wasn't loud it resonated through the small house. "I tried to deliver this message to many people, but they were blind to me. "[PARAGRAPH]"Who are you?" Amelie asked. She wondered if she was dreaming, but it seemed both too real and too unlikely to be a dream. [PARAGRAPH]"I am Verchiel, herald angel of Lugus. I have come to send a message, and a warning. " the angel answered. "Your brother Artan is in great danger. He has left your house and wandered into darkness. He is already beyond my sight, and it may not be possible to save him. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie sat up in her bed. The sudden skip and racing of her heart convinced her that she was not asleep. "Where is he? What kind of danger?" she asked. [PARAGRAPH]"He is within the home of an Anointedor, out of the light and into the province of the god of blood. " Seeing that Amelie was confused Verchiel added, "He is in the home of an evil man. That is all I know. Lugus's influence is waning and I have very little ability to act. You may be able to save your brother, you may not, or you may die in the attempt. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie was already out of bed throwing on her shoes and coat. [PARAGRAPH]"Where is he?" Amelie asked. [PARAGRAPH]"He went to the candy shop. " Verchiel said, and for a second the angel looked afraid. Before Amelie rushed out of her room Verchiel stopped her. "I can give some small help. If you get to the temple and you hold your hand on the altar you will be safe. It is the most I can offer, though it is not much. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie rushed out of her room and into Artan's. Just as the angel said Artan was gone. His blankets were thrown aside, and his shoes and coat were missing. Amelie went back into the hall where she noticed her room was dark again, the angel was gone. But she didn't stop to consider his disappearance as she ran into her father's room. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie's father snored loudly from his bed. His lamp flickered and cast odd shadows. The room smelled like stale beer and sweat. Amelie shouted at her father, called for him, and shook him. But in his drunken delirium he did nothing but swat her away. Amelie pushed him off the bed. He crashed to the floor in a tangle of blankets, rolled over and continued snoring. Giving up, Amelie left him and headed outside onto a small landing and down the stairs to the street. [PARAGRAPH]It was an early winter night and the season's first light snowfall was settling on the city. Amelie could see her brother's tracks in the snow and she followed them along the street toward the candy shop. [PARAGRAPH]The candy shop was only a few blocks away and it appeared as it did on all their visits. It was tidier than the surrounding buildings, and its red roof and white trim seemed at odds with the fear that clawed at Amelie as she ran. Though the front room of the shop was lost in darkness Amelie imagined that there were still rows of jars full of candy, and for a second she thought herself crazy for having rushed here in a panic. Until she noticed her brother's footprints leading up to the front porch. [PARAGRAPH]She followed them onto the porch with her heart once again racing. The roof kept the porch clear of snow, Artan's footprints ended at the porch stairs. Amelie crossed the porch, and though she had never noticed that the porch creaked in the many times she walked across it, now it seemed to cry out with each step. [PARAGRAPH]Reaching the door, she turned the knob, but it was locked. It seemed secure and untampered with. Unless someone had locked it since Artan went in, Amelie couldn't imagine how he would have gotten through. [PARAGRAPH]Walking down the porch Amelie came to the large front window. Pushing her face against the glass she looked into the room beyond. She could see the vague outlines of the room. The counter where the sales were made, the shelves covered in candy jars. What wasn't lost in darkness seemed normal. [PARAGRAPH]For the first time Amelie shivered in the cold. Though her coat was warm, she had thrown it on over her sleeping gown, which was one of her father's old shirts. It was threadbare before she got it and though it hung just past her knees, it provided little protection against the chill night air. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie walked to the end of the porch looking for anything unusual. At the very end she saw where Artan's footprints began again. He had jumped off the porch and walked around the side of the shop. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie followed the footprints around into the darkness. She had to stop and wait for her eyes to adjust, and build up her courage. There was no one on the street, but as she stood in the shop's shadow Amelie remembered that there was a guard station at the north bridge a few blocks away. If she ran there and if the guards believed her she could be back with help in fifteen, maybe twenty minutes. Deciding Artan may not be able to wait that long, she continued following the footprints around the shop. [PARAGRAPH]The back of the shop was a simple deep green wall with white trim and no doors. There was a small window set too high in the wall for Amelie to see through. But it wasn't the window or the shop that interested her, but what the tracks led to, a simple cellar door in the ground. [PARAGRAPH]The bar that usually blocked the cellar door now lay discarded beside it. Though Artan's footprints clearly led to the cellar door, there was no indication of him walking away. Amelie whispered a prayer to Lugus as she walked to the door, then hoping it was quieter than the squeaky porch, she opened it. [PARAGRAPH]Beneath the door a ladder descended into darkness. Amelie could feel warm, moist air coming out of the cellar and she was happy to see that there was a faint flickering light below. Leaning close to the opening Amelie whispered for Artan, trying to be loud enough so he would hear her, but quiet enough that someone else wouldn't. [PARAGRAPH]After waiting to see if there was any sound or response, Amelie climbed into the hole and down into the cellar. Cellars were unusual in Bourne, as the city sat between two rivers the ground was generally too wet to dig down in. Any sufficiently deep hole turned into a well. But the few she had seen had stairs leading into them, not ladders. And this ladder went down further than Amelie expected. If the candy shop had a basement, Amelie guessed that this cellar would be below it. [PARAGRAPH]The ladder ended at a hallway with a rough stone floor and slick reddish-brown walls. The ladder shaft was so small that an adult would have difficulty squeezing through, but the hallway was much larger. Looking up Amelie could see the night sky, and now that she was on the ground she could see light coming from further down the hallway. After whispering again for Artan and receiving no response she started slowly down the hallway. [PARAGRAPH]A scream echoed through the cellar so pained and shocked that Amelie nearly turned and fled back up the ladder. She couldn't imagine a person could communicate such horror in a yell, and at first thought it wasn't human. But her body went chill as she recognized the voice, it was Artan. [PARAGRAPH]Everything seemed to slow down. The smallest details leapt out at her and even though Amelie ran down the short hallway toward the screams, she felt like she was running in mud. [PARAGRAPH]The hallway continued straight with two open archways on each side. A lit lamp hung on a hook between the archways and provided the only light. Amelie only briefly glimpsed through the first two archways as she rushed by, the left contained large cages, like a kennel. Something moved in the cages, something large and covered in filth. The opposite archway was dominated by a stone table and tools and knives hung from the walls. Both rooms made Amelie more afraid. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie ran into the second room on the right, where Artan's screams were coming from. For a moment she was delighted to see that Artan stood in the middle of the room facing away from her, appearing uninjured. Amelie grabbed him and spun him around, pulling him into a hug. He jumped when she touched him and tried to push away, but as soon as he realized it was her he collapsed against her and burst into heavy, pained sobs. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie didn't have to ask why he was crying. What was hanging on the wall stole any slight relief Amelie may have felt at the recovery of her brother. [PARAGRAPH]Once it had been a man, a massively fat man buried in rolls of flesh. But all the fat had been cut away. His chest lay open, brass eyelets had been sewn into his skin and hooks held open a bloody gaping maw that exposed the bare organs beneath. His organs were tied along his spinal column and his heart still beat from within a thin mesh of netting, his lungs expanded and shrank with each breath and the slick bloody mass of organs dumped down into coiled intestines. His lower jaw and tongue had been removed so his head was a helpless hook on the wall, and his eyes moved and watched the children with an emotion Amelie had never seen before. His arms and legs had been painfully hollowed out, leaving the bone and clinging muscle, but now only air filled the loose skin. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie opened her mouth to scream but no sound came out. [PARAGRAPH]The crack of the cellar door closing shocked Amelie into action. [PARAGRAPH]"Shut up!" she yelled at Artan, "Are you okay?" As she asked, Amelie made sure Artan stayed facing her, so he couldn't see the man hanging on the wall behind him. [PARAGRAPH]Taking deep breaths Artan coughed out his words, "I. . . want. . . to. . . go. "[PARAGRAPH]"We will be okay, calm down. I am going to take you home. " Amelie said. The man hanging on the wall continued to stare at her and Amelie wondered if he had snuck down into the cellar looking for sweets too. [PARAGRAPH]The sound of another door opening and slamming closed shocked them both. It sounded closer than the cellar door. Amelie guessed it was from whatever was straight down the hallway. She could hear someone walking toward them. It was the familiar step, step, click of the candy shop owner's cane. [PARAGRAPH]Holding Artan close Amelie dove beneath the only object in the room besides the hanging man. It was a small end table near the entrance to the room. She could hear the footsteps in the hall. She held Artan's head against her chest and tried to stay quiet. She looked at the hanging man, silently pleading with him to quit staring at where they were hiding. [PARAGRAPH]The lamp light jumped and flickered as someone lifted the lamp off its hook. Then Amelie saw Hamish's wiry legs and cane step in beside the end table. She and Artan held their breath in fear. She briefly considered rushing to Hamish for help. But nothing in the candy shop owner's demeanor seemed surprised by the man hanging on the wall, and that kept Amelie trembling and quiet beneath the end table. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish set the lamp down on top of the end table, and walked across the room to look at the hanging man. With Hamish's back to them Amelie considered running from the room. As Amelie watched, Hamish set his cane down. Then he climbed up onto the hanging man and spun around, sliding his legs down into the partially hollow legs of the hanging man and his arms into the huge bodies hollow arms. Hamish's head came just under the hanging man's upper jaw, so it appeared that Hamish was wearing the hanging man's horrified face as a cruel helmet. The hanging man only offered a muffled cry in protest, but Hamish ignored him. Instead Hamish looked delighted to be settling into the hanging man's body, wearing a living man as a thick fleshy suit. The candy maker's eyes sparkled as he ran a cord through the brass eyelets, sewing himself into the body so that only his head remained exposed. [PARAGRAPH]Too terrified to see what would happen when Hamish finished sewing himself into the body Amelie crawled out from under the end table and pulled Artan behind her. She grabbed the lamp off the end table and ran into the hallway, back toward the shaft up to the cellar door. She pushed Artan in front of her and he climbed up the ladder shaft into the darkness. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie was halfway up the ladder before she heard Hamish thundering down the hallway after them. This time there was no slow click of the cane, only thick pounding footfalls. She looked down at the pudgy flesh of the hanging man's hands and arms as Hamish grabbed the ladder and shook it. But they were almost at the top. [PARAGRAPH]Artan reached the top and tried to swing the cellar door open, but it had been barred from the outside. [PARAGRAPH]"It's locked!" Artan yelled. [PARAGRAPH] The ladder shook again as Hamish was tearing it off the wall. Both the children screamed, hoping someone outside would hear them. [PARAGRAPH]"Hold onto the sides. " Amelie yelled as the ladder threatened to collapse. [PARAGRAPH]"Come down children. " Hamish called, "You will be ripe fruit on Aeron's altar tonight. "[PARAGRAPH]At that the ladder collapsed and Amelie and Artan were left braced in the shaft. Artan slipped on the wet walls. Below them Hamish laughed in delight. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm sorry. " Artan said, and his eyes began to well up with tears. [PARAGRAPH]"Listen to me. " Amelie ordered, "Is there another door?"[PARAGRAPH]"Yes," Artan said, "straight down the hallway there are stairs leading up. But that door is barred too. "[PARAGRAPH]"I don't think so, not anymore. He couldn't have barred this door from the outside if he came down it. He had to have come through the other door. " Amelie said. She could feel herself slipping. Hamish had become quiet, but he still glared up at them with hungry, depraved eyes. [PARAGRAPH]"When I say go," Amelie said, "slide down the shaft as fast as you can and run for that door. Don't stop for anything. Just run and go to the temple, not home. In the temple put your hand on the altar and don't take it off until you are safe, he can't hurt you if you touch the altar. Do you understand?"[PARAGRAPH]Artan nodded. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie took one more look down at Hamish, then she dropped the lamp. [PARAGRAPH]The lamp smashed into the hallway floor and oil splashed out in all directions, burning Hamish and setting the entire base of the shaft on fire. [PARAGRAPH]"Go!" Amelie yelled. [PARAGRAPH]Together they slid down the ladder shaft and Amelie hit the burning cellar floor hard. Artan landed on top of her and she immediately pushed him up onto his feet. The grotesque form of Hamish was slapping at itself trying to put the fire out and though he nearly filled the hallway Artan was quickly up and past him. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie slipped in the burning oil and fell when she tried to run. Her coat caught fire and when she got up again Hamish was on her. Hamish grabbed her sleeve and pulled her against the bare skin of his living suit. Amelie could feel the dank sweat of the hanging man, could smell his rotting flesh and looked up to see two pairs of eyes staring back at her. Hamish's sparkled with dark pleasure, and the hanging man looked equally horrified and helpless. [PARAGRAPH]Artan came running back down the hall. He had one of the knives from the room with the stone table in his hand. Before Hamish turned Artan leapt at him, stabbing clear through the hanging man's back and into Hamish. [PARAGRAPH]The jolt of pain was enough for Amelie to unfasten her coat and slip out of Hamish's grip. She ran by him, grabbing Artan as she went. [PARAGRAPH]They ran past the four archways to where stairs lead up into darkness. Hamish thundered down the hallway behind them and his elongated shadow was reflected on every surface by the fire burning under the ladder shaft. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie could barely make out a closed door at the top of the stairs and she prayed as she charged toward it that it would open. She hit it full speed and it flew open. [PARAGRAPH]Both children popped up into a long kitchen. A pot boiled in a fireplace, ovens were set against one wall and tables were covered with trays and bowls. A tray of freshly baked cookies sat out, half covered in green frosting. The room smelled of gingerbread and vanilla. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie and Artan were stunned by the change in scenery. The room seemed cozy and welcoming, homey in a way their home had never been. But the sound of Hamish on the stairs reminded them they were still in danger. [PARAGRAPH]"Close the door!" Amelie yelled. [PARAGRAPH]Artan swung the door closed while Amelie searched for the bar used to brace it. She found it on the counter nearest the door and raced to slide it through the four iron braces on the back of the door. It had only gone through the first when Hamish hit the door. [PARAGRAPH]For a brief second the door looked like it may hold, but then, in an explosion of splintering wood, the door flew open and Hamish came stumbling up into the kitchen. Once again, the children were off running. Artan threw open the door on the far end of the kitchen, revealing a short hallway that ended at a room the children recognized, the front room of the candy shop. [PARAGRAPH]They ran through the front room, past the shelves of jars and treats they had dreamed about for so long. Artan went to the front door, but Amelie ran to the low bench in front of the window. [PARAGRAPH]The door was locked. [PARAGRAPH]"Help me. " Amelie yelled as she lifted one end of the bench. [PARAGRAPH]Artan grabbed the other end and as Hamish entered the front room the children threw the bench through the huge front window. Amelie and Artan leapt through the shattered window behind it. [PARAGRAPH]The children screamed for help as they ran up the hill toward the temple. Hamish continued his pursuit, and though the glass shards cut up the hanging man's feet, he raced after them. If he had looked crazed in the nightmare of the cellar, he looked even more so in the ordinary city night. A man wearing another man's body as a second skin running through the streets of Bourne. [PARAGRAPH]Despite his cut feet Hamish was faster than the children on the straight road. And if anyone heard the calls for help, they weren't responding. [PARAGRAPH]By the time Amelie reached the temple, her terror had been replaced with exhaustion. She could barely breathe, she felt like she was choking, and her heart was racing so fast it made her dizzy. Amelie collapsed against the temple door and turned the handle, for the first time wondering if the temple would even be unlocked. [PARAGRAPH]It was unlocked, but where Amelie expected the warm glow of safety or an army of priests and angels set to protect them, there was only the cold, lifeless interior of the temple. The pews were empty and the stained-glass windows dark. The clear round window that formed the top of the church was the only real source of light. Through it moonlight shone down on the center of the temple, highlighting the altar. [PARAGRAPH]"Put your hand on the altar and don't let go. " Amelie commanded. [PARAGRAPH]Artan looked less convinced, his eyes widened in fear when he realized this door was the only way into, or out of, the temple. They would be trapped here. [PARAGRAPH]There was no time to try to close the door behind them, Hamish was in the doorway right behind them. As the children ran to the center of the small temple Hamish stopped to look around. It seemed that he may also have expected some sort of defense here, though he was obviously pleased to see that the temple was empty. He closed the temple door behind him. [PARAGRAPH]"For a moment I thought you might get away. " Hamish said smiling. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish stretched in the hanging man's skin, the sight was grotesque and unnerving. Bones creaked and popped and the cord binding the chest together pulled taunt against the loose flesh. Above Hamish's head the hanging man's eyes fluttered back and forth in fear as if looking for something in the room. [PARAGRAPH]"You can't hurt us here. " Amelie said, her hand firmly on the Altar's warm mahogany top. [PARAGRAPH]"Are we playing some of game?" Hamish asked, "Is this your base? I'm afraid I may have to break the rules. "[PARAGRAPH]Hamish walked down the center aisle toward them. [PARAGRAPH]"You dropped this. " Hamish said, holding out Amelie's burnt coat. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie didn't move. Artan fidgeted beside her, he still held the knife with one hand and gripped the altar with the other. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm glad you followed your brother. " Hamish said, "You will make a wonderful offering. And I can keep your brother to fatten up. "[PARAGRAPH]At that Hamish charged the altar. Just before Hamish hit them Artan let go of the altar and stepped in front of his sister, swinging wildly with his knife. [PARAGRAPH]"No!" Amelie screamed, grabbing Artan's free hand. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish caught Artan's knife hand in a fist so large it nearly covered up Artan's entire forearm. Hamish pushed down on the back of Artan's hand with his thumb, forcing him to drop the knife, then with a sickening pop Artan's wrist broke. [PARAGRAPH]Artan screamed in pain. And though Amelie pulled, her brother was caught between them. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish towered over the children, Amelie barely came to his waist and as Hamish pulled the screaming Artan away, Amelie's finger slid easily across the smooth altar. She stretched as her fingers came to the edge of the altar. Just as her fingertips were all that was left of her contact with the altar she let go of Artan's hand. [PARAGRAPH]"Shhh. . . " Hamish whispered to the crying boy. Hamish lifted Artan, placing one meaty hand over Artan's mouth. Three sets of eyes looked down at Amelie, but she stood unmoving, hand once again firmly on the altar. Tears silently pouring down her face. [PARAGRAPH]Without saying anything Hamish turned and walked out of the temple, carrying the struggling Artan with him. When he was gone Amelie collapsed beside the altar, with her hand still on it, and cried so violently that her small body shook with each wail and ragged coughing breath. That is where they found her the next morning, though Hamish and Artan were gone.

The Foxmen are a cult of Tali, God of the Wind. He has no formal priesthood but many shrines built in the most remote and dangerous parts of Erebus. Some say the Foxmen put them there just to give each other excuses to travel. The Foxmen are renowned for their Wanderlust. They cannot stand to stay still for very long. There are no better explorers than their Drifters, nor better story tellers. The closest thing to a mass religious service are the convocations that they Foxmen are known to hold on the rooftops of popular inns, where they regale each other with tall tales of their past or future exploits. Ceridwen, Goddess of the Stars, of Magic,and of the Social Relationships that bind mortals together, is served by numerous cults with only tenuous ties to one another. [PARAGRAPH:2]Ceridwen first appeared to a suicidal Kylorin, asking him to worship her in exchange for arcane knowledge and the power to resurrect his wife indefinitely so they might restart their marriage untainted by her adultery. He attempted to make her cult into the State Religion of Patria, but only a small group of elites ever accepted her tenets. The most elite of the elites were the Coven of the Black Candle, whom she tasked with blotting out The Sun. This Coven consisted of Kylorin himself, Os-Gabella, Asmoday, Faeryl Viconia, Alexis, Barbatos, and "Wode"-who was actually the God of Shadow masquerading as the mortal master of Shadow magic. Esus transformed his Seven Aspects (the greatest of his True Angels besides Iaegus) into the Masks each Coven member wore, so that no power in creation could detect or control them. The members could never learn each other's identity, as the animus between Asmoday and the Fey would have made their cooperation impossible. [PARAGRAPH:1]A lesser Masked Coven, called "The Between," continues to this day. It is a small religion whose members are mostly sorceresses whose spirits, minds and occasionally bodies explore worlds beyond Erebus. Many are driven mad by the experience. They refer to their goddesses as the Maiden of the Mask. [PARAGRAPH:1]Among the Sheaim there is a cult filled with a missionary zeal to reach all nations and bring their best and brightest back to learn sorcery without the strictures and limitations placed on adepts by mage guilds in all other lands. They promise unfettered access to secret knowledge of all sorts, but tend to steer their students into the darkest of arts. The Emrys have a goal more grand that blotting our the son. They want to bring on Armageddon and end Erebus entirely. [PARAGRAPH:1]Not all of her worshipers are that evil. The Chainbreakers have more noble goals. They believe the goddess is best served by breaking unjust social bonds. They hate any relationship that is not entirely consensual. Some try to destroy marriages and turn children against their parents, but most focus their radical activism on fighting for the abolition of slavery. They can always be counted upon to provide aid and sanctuary to runaway slaves, but prefer to give them arms and help them slay their former masters. Deep with the richest areas of the world (and only those areas) great temples to Amathaon provide rest and an endless bounty to those that would join them. They are less about worship and more about providing hospitality, like the world's best bed and breakfast. Often called the Lord of Plenty.

The Ring-givers' faith is practiced through artifice. Each accomplishment or blessing is added to their collection of charms, rings and baubles. Judges sought out to adjudicate between different parties. Their religion preaches against bias and imparts decisions without local or personal influence. Mechanic: The Grey Council is a voting body where the player can participate in elections with other players. Often called the Adjudicator.

The church of Bhall has little long-lasting structure. Instead religious upheavals happen and huge masses of fanatical followers rise up and rebel against whatever is being protested in that area. The cause is less important than the fervor, the blessing of Bhall, and the violence that comes with the rebellion. Most worshipers of Bhall receive a brand of her mark that forever burns and inflicts pain. Bhall is also known as the Queen of Fire and the Fallen Star.

The church of Camulos wants war between all nations. He is known as the Sanguine Fountain and the Hundred Armed God. On the nights before large battles, the skies echo with the shrill cries of Camulos's demons, peering out expectantly for the coming war. In cities that don't outlaw them, temples to Camulos are brutal arenas where corpses of the freshly killed lie in piles, feral animals feast on the bodies, and nearly every stone is blood stained. This is a religion based on hate. It is racist in some countries, anti-cultural group in others. The target doesn't matter to the religion, only the hate that is fueled by it.

[TAB]Junil, the elder of the Gods, had promised to stay apart from the conflict in Creation. While other gods pressed the limits of the Compact or blatantly ignored it, he held to its restrictions and spirit. Even when his church was a mockery of his dominion, he would not respond. It was only when the compact was openly broken, when fallen angels walked in creation that he responded to help the least of men. He asked only one thing in return: unquestioning obedience. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Order was founded during the Age of Magic, not from divine inspiration but from the growing requirements of the Patrian bureaucracy. The codex of Patrian law had become so byzantine and severe that nearly autonomous inquisitors were needed to carry out it requirements. These inquisitors were magically bound to the codex so that they wouldn't become corrupted by their station. They drew upon the name of Junil, God of Law, in taking their oaths and in carrying out their brutal decrees. [PARAGRAPH:1]These inquisitors were feared nearly as much as Kylorin's Archmages and would come to a city to adjudicate major disputes and to see that justice, as defined by the codex of Patria, was followed. [PARAGRAPH:1]At the head of the church was Soqed Hozi. It is said that if she spoke a lie, reality would change to make it into truth. Soqed had a mute twin who was little more than a dim shadow of her powerful sister. The two remained at the Temple of Atonement where they oversaw the church and its inquisitors. [PARAGRAPH:1]The ideology of Junil was secondary to the church's task of maintaining the laws of Patria. Some lesser confessors began to question: "What was the use of following the law if it was corrupt?". The most conflicted of these was Sphener, an inquisitor who killed demons in his service to the church. He had gazed into hell and it was only his strict adherence to his faith that allowed him to survive. Sphener obeyed every edict of the church, but argued that worship of Junil was the greatest mission of the church. [PARAGRAPH:1]The church found out about the whispered concerns of some of its members and launched the Purge of Whispers, and attempt to execute anyone in the church who questioned church doctrine. [PARAGRAPH:1]The purge was horribly effective and killed members of the church, family and friends. It covered many cities over all of Patria and happened in a single night. Sphener was one of the few that escaped the purge and the next day the church held a trial for him in absentia. They convicted him and sentenced him to death upon the wheel. Condemned by his law, his church, and his god, Sphener came to the church on his own and accepted his execution. He was broken as the church elders and the public watched. [PARAGRAPH:1]Over the next decade Sphener's spirit was seen hundreds of times tending to those in need. He tended to those unfairly persecuted by the church and ministered to church members that prayed to Junil for guidance. This became the basis for the new Order church that would be founded in the Age of Rebirth. [TAB]Where the Order values law, the Empyrean values wisdom. Adjudication started from the teachings of Lugus and punishment is not based on adherence to a labyrinthine codex of laws, but from direct consultation on the merits of each case. Social equality and impartiality are the model between a government and its citizens as well as between empires. As such the Empyrean gives equal voice to small empires as it does those that dominate Erebus. [TAB]Kilmorph is the goddess of the earth, She Who Dwells Beneath. She formed children out of stone, the Dwarves, and taught them the secrets of metalworking. One of the first religions available to the men of the world, Kilmorph will answer the prayers of honorable men and even send her soldiers to defend their cities. [TAB]The power beneath the Aegean waves is said to be more powerful than any other, but the Undertow are unfocused and follow a thousand different obscure agendas. The Disciples of the Undertow dare not expose themselves directly to the conflicting commands of their masters and instead use the poor as intermediaries. They are quickly driven insane by the process, which the disciples prefer as it keeps them from manipulating the message. They also share the process of turning a warrior into The Drown, undead thralls, a process with few volunteers. [TAB]A secret council that is so good at spreading lies that it is often unaware of the truth of its own stories. They have "thrones" (secret meeting places) in most major cities and excel at sneaking goods and people into or out of areas. Esus is known as the King of Thieves, Jack Shadow, and Moonsong, though it's popular for religious leaders to take these names for themselves as well. [PARAGRAPH:2]Founding[PARAGRAPH]This is the most common legend spread about the founding of the religion. No one knows if it's actually true. [PARAGRAPH]Unknown to the other gods, Esus slips into creation from time to time. Most commonly as a traveling minstrel (male or female as it suits him), but occasionally as a merchant, beggar, jackal or crow. [PARAGRAPH]On one of these trips he met Oriol Peregrinus, a priest of Kilmorph who had been stealing from his temple for years. The night before he was to go face trial he sat in a bar drinking and whispering prayers to any god that would hear him, as his own certainly wouldn't forgive his crime. [PARAGRAPH]Esus, who was playing at the bar, overheard him and went to comfort the man. The two shared drinks and eventually Oriol shared his story. Esus offered a lie that Oriol could tell to the church, but Oriol was still worried that he wouldn't be believed. At that Esus offered him an opal scarab that would make anyone believe his lies. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol took the scarab and went to his trial before the church elders. To his surprise, they believed his lies without question. Those that accused him were punished and it increased his standing in the church of Kilmorph. [PARAGRAPH]A year later Esus returned and found Oriol at the bar again. This time he was ruined, he barely had the money to pay for his drink and had lost everything in the world that mattered to him. Esus asked what was wrong and he said that no one believed anything he said. He thought the scarab was cursed and threw it away. [PARAGRAPH]Esus explained that he had made the man's lies believable, but at a cost that no one would believe anything Oriol said that was true. If Oriol told his wife he loved her, she wouldn't believe him. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol sobbed into his drink. [PARAGRAPH]"What is your name?" Esus asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Oriol. " Oriol said, still staring into his drink. [PARAGRAPH]"I don't believe you. " Esus said. "I think your name is Mendax Opacous. "[PARAGRAPH]"My name is Mendax?" Oriol asked. [PARAGRAPH]"That sounds better. That is a name people will believe. " Esus said. "And what god do you worship? Surely not Kilmorph, I think you worship Esus, the god of shadows. "[PARAGRAPH]"I worship the god of shadows?" Oriol asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Yes you do. See how easy this is. " Esus said. "And remember that you can tell any woman you love her, and she will believe you. As long as it isn't true. If you actually love her then your words will be sour to her ears, your affections will poison her against you. You can go to a new city, start a new life, raise up a church to Esus, as long as you know that it is all pretend. "[PARAGRAPH]"I have already lost my wife's love to your curse. " Oriol said. "I have lost my standing in the church, you should have me abandon my faith as well? What if I just go to church elders and tell them about what you have done to me?"[PARAGRAPH]"You could try, but who would believe you?" Esus said with a smile. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol, now going by Mendax, did as Esus suggested and founded the first Aphotic Throne in an abandoned Patrian manor (it was easy enough to convince them that he was the real owner). The traditions of that throne were largely made up by him in a tangled weave of whatever inspiration struck him in the moment. It was said that his biggest secret was that he kept a small shrine of Kilmorph until the day he died. [PARAGRAPH:3]Sects[PARAGRAPH]Every Throne could be considered its own sect. There is no common communication, rules or traditions between them. Some are brutal and vengeful, others are lighthearted and free. They tend to be the opposite of the communities they exist in. Sometimes they are the secret power behind the city government, and sometimes they are teenage adventurers pretending at being a secret organization. [PARAGRAPH:3]An oddity among the religions, the Council of Esus has no temples or ordinary disciples. As a secret society, it cannot be [LINK=SPELL_EVANGELIZE]Evangelized[\LINK] openly to either cities or all the units nearby. However, any unit which is a member can pay to establish a local Council presence in any city. Units without another State Religion prerequisite, and with a leader with the right State Religion, can spend gold to purchase an initiation from an Esus [LINK=PROMOTION_EVANGELIZE]Evangelist[\LINK] on the same plot. That theme, paying for miracles, is common in the Council of Esus. [PARAGRAPH]Esus's priests have the abilities of Spies, including the ability to steal plans, destroy city production, and sabotage improvements including even Unique Features. [PARAGRAPH]State Religion allows access to the [LINK=UNIT_SHADOWRIDER]Shadowrider[\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_DISCIPLE_ESUS]Swindler [\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_ESUS]Thief[\LINK], and [LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_ESUS]Propogandist[\LINK] units. [PARAGRAPH]The Council of Esus has major conflicts with The Empyrean. One may prevent the spread of another into a city, or drive the other out. [PARAGRAPH]The Council of Esus was the driving force behind the founding of the Undercouncil in opposition to the Overcouncil. No player may adopt the Undercouncil civic until this religion is founded, nor may any player with this state religion join the Overcouncil.

Its arda will be weakened by [LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]The Children of The One[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]The Matronae[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]The Grey Council[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_UNBLEMISHED]The Unblemished[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]The Ringgivers[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Order[\LINK], the [LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]The Runes of Kilmorph[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]Cult of the Dragon[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]The House of Plenty[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]The Brotherhood of Wardens[\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_FELLOWSHIP_OF_LEAVES]The Fellowship of the Leaves[\LINK]. It will be weakened in Good lands, strengthened in Neutral or Evil lands.It will be strengthened by proximity to [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SHADOW]Shadow Mana[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WODES_OAK]Wode's Oak[\LINK], and the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WHISPERING_WOOD]Whispering Wood[\LINK], It is weakened by [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SUN]Sun Mana[\LINK], the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MIRROR_OF_HEAVEN]Mirror of Heaven[\LINK], and [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITADEL_OF_LIGHT]Citadels of Light[\LINK].

[TAB]Mages spent weeks in meditation, exploring the farthest reaches of the ethereal world. The demands of the body were ignored, and they survived sustained only by magic. Their efforts were rewarded, a sentience was contacted, dark and horrible. It whispered secrets into the mages' minds, secrets of necromancy, diseases, and sacrificial rites. It promised power in exchange for their blood, and they freely gave it.
