It will be weakened in Good and strengthened in Evil lands. It will be strengthened by proximity to [LINK=BONUS_MANA_ENTROPY]Entropy Mana[\LINK] and weakened by [LINK=BONUS_MANA_CREATION]Creation Mana[\LINK]. It is strenthened near [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_GRAVE_OF_ASMODAY]the Grave of Asmoday[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_HELLFIRE]Hellfire[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_PIT]Pits of Torment[\LINK], and [LINK=FEATURE_TORMENTED_SOULS]Tormented Souls[\LINK], and weakened on [LINK=FEATURE_HALLOWED_GROUND]Hallowed Ground[\LINK].

[TAB]Thus spoke the Martyr Mishahel, as the Luonnotar stood chained in the city plaza awaiting Junil's justice: [PARAGRAPH:1]"You ask us to repent? We ask you the same. We are all Children of The One, you, and I, and all your so-called gods alike, no matter who denies it. His angels may have made this world, but only by His leave. This warrants them no worship. We will adore only The One. The Twenty-One have all sinned and fallen short of the glory of The One, by far more than the vilest mortal falls short of your Junil's majesty. Our Elder Brothers, the angels, swore to guide us to enlightenment, to make us all their equals. Instead, like petulant children, they have turned their charges into pawns for petty squabbles among themselves. Now it falls to us to enlighten them. Fighting evil with evil can never be called justice. Junil is no better than Agares, only a greater hypocrite. Every "god" willing joined Agares' rebellion. They are all oath-breakers. The All-Father offered his children true freedom, but from fear and lust for power they have chosen bondage. Agares stole the Gems of Creation and forged their links to the infinite planes, but each "god" gladly enslaved his own soul to his to a separate precept. Our own sire, Nemed, came near to redemption when he surrendered his divinity, but in his folly defied The One and damned us all to "immortality. " Only The One should last forever. I endure only by his will. This world soon shall pass away. We will all be judged. Perhaps some shall escape Creation and enter into the True Heaven. Repent now while there is still a chance, lest you instead be punished along with your idols. "[PARAGRAPH:2]With this their trial was over. The Priors had heard enough. Such egregious blasphemy demanded special punishment. Hanging or decapitation would not suffice. These fools must be made an example to the public in the most dramatic way: a Pillar of Fire called down from the heavens. The Pontiff's prayers had been answered with the miracle on multiple occasions during the late war against The Ashen Veil, and he knew Junil would be eager to purge this greater scourge. [PARAGRAPH:2]Junil indeed hated the gospel of the Luonnotar, because he feared it might be true. How could any mortal know such things? The terms of The Compact forbid any angel from sharing such secrets with the living. One worry filled his soul with terror: could The One have returned, and revealed himself only to these mortals? Impossible. . . or was it? Junil was now forced to doubt his own righteousness. Was not Agares first great sin the creation of a world and people required to worship him, and kept in ignorance of the truth? This line of thought would have gone on, until he recalled an obscure clause that Dagda's Archangel had inserted into The Compact which precisely dictated his proper course action. He suppressed his existential angst by following the letter of the law as usual. [PARAGRAPH:2]The people watched in awe as they saw the flames descending from the sky, with greater force than had ever descended before. The Prior was certain of his victory, while the Luonnotar stoically accepted their unjust fate. No one predicted what came next. The pillar descended and engulfed them, but not a hair on their heads or a fiber of their clothing was singed. The same could not be said of the chains binding them, or the flesh of their persecutors, or the stones of the Basilica itself, which rapidly melted away. Half the city cried in anguish, and were reduced to ash. The only survivors within miles of the plaza were the condemned, and those who had hearkened to their words. [PARAGRAPH]Rumors spread that the basilica was burned by sorcery, and armies amassed to avenge the massacre. Assailed at every stop, the Luonnotar always proved invulnerable to divine magic yet often fell to mundane blades. They continued to preach and attract new converts, but were always on the verge of extinction until finding sanctuary among the Grigori. Cassiel sent word assuring them that they could live in peace within his realm so long as they never tried to emulate their persecutors. Refugees of all faiths were welcome to live in peace among the Grigori, if they could tolerate that blasphemy was the national pastime. The Luonnotar gained a base from which to organize evangelism abroad, but rarely won converts among their skeptical new compatriots. Mishahel continued to petition the fallen archangel for an audience and for some endorsement for his beliefs, but was always ignored. The one blasphemy Cassiel cannot tolerate is the notion that The One is petty enough to desire any cult of worshipers. [PARAGRAPH:3]The Children of The One religion may start in either one two ways: through a random event that may occur in any city under any state religion, or the Grigori civilization discovering [LINK=TECH_ARCANE_LORE]Arcane Lore[\LINK]. [PARAGRAPH]Cities with this and another faith are both present have a chance of triggering a Monotheist Revolt, in which this faith will force its competitors out. If the religion removed was a state religion, then the city will revolt as if newly conquered. The Children of The One itself can never be a state religion. [PARAGRAPH]The [LINK=UNIT_LUONNOTAR]Luonnotar[\LINK], the religion's only unique unit, can travel through rival territory without open boarder agreements in order to spread its faith among cities and units alike. Priests of other religions who adopt this faith are defrocked--the units are automatically deleted if anyone tries to use them. The Luonnotar unit is immune to magic and has no spells of its own, but is very strong against disciple units and will target them even in stacks with better defenders. Any unit which converts to this religion becomes [LINK=PROMOTION_MAGIC_RESISTANCE]resistant to magic[\LINK] and also [LINK=PROMOTION_REBEL]rebellious[\LINK] against any owner that is running any state religion. If a leader with a state religion orders such units to fight against the Grigori, they will most likely defect. The religion's only building is its holy shrine, [LINK=BUILDING_UNHARMED_MARTYRS]The Unmarred Martyrs[\LINK]. This provides [LINK=BONUS_MANA_FORCE]Force mana[\LINK], great person points towards [LINK=UNIT_ADVENTURER]Adventurers[\LINK], and increased war weariness for your enemies. Units in the city are 100% resistant to magic, gain the Scourge promotion, and lose the [LINK=PROMOTION_DIVINE]Divine[\LINK] promotion (priests loose access to their spells just by passing through the city). It makes other religious buildings cause a great deal of unhappiness. [PARAGRAPH]Units of this religion will never return as either [LINK=UNIT_ANGEL]Angels[\LINK] or [LINK=UNIT_MANES]Manes[\LINK]. [PARAGRAPH:3]All priests have their Ardas weakened by the presence of the Children of the One, especially in cities nearby. Once the Children of the One have enough influence, priests may abandon their faith and become rebellious, possibly disbanding themselves of defecting to the Grigori.

[TAB]There have been men have worshiped The White Hand of Mulcarn in every era since before the time of the Godswar, but they have never been many. During the Age of Magic, his stoic Frost Speakers were tolerated but disrespected. Mulcarn was considered the least of the gods, at a time when his nemesis Bhall was considered the greatest. Although the least evil of all those who sided with Agares against The One, he was a supremely jealous god who grew to greatly hate humanity for their devotion to every god but himself. As Nostalgia is his very nature, he longed to return to how things were in the Godswar, when man was a primitive being subject to the whims of the divine and gods were not bound by the regulations of The Compact. [TAB]The Fall of Bhall gave him an opportunity to make this a reality. With no god to oppose him, he was able to maneuver the one people who honored him, the nearly destitute Illians, into completing a ritual that summoned him into the plane of Erebus. Sucellus was sent to enforce The Compact and prevent Mulcarn's conquest of the world, but he failed in his endeavor. His body was broken in seven pieces and buried in distant regions of the infinite plane, to prevent them from being reunited and allowing his spirit to return from the Netherworld to challenge The God of Winter again. Where a god failed, and man succeeded. Kylorin, Archmage of the Seventh Circle and former Emperor of All Mankind, was sent on a mission by Nantosuelta (the Goddess of Enchantment and Virtue, who loved Sucellus greatly) to end The Age of Ice and retrieve the Heart of Sucellus from within Mulcarn's citadel. (She had already managed to have the other six pieces of his body gathered together. ) He gathered and reforged the pieces of the Godslayer, a weapon created as a symbol and manifestation of The Compact, and destroyed Mulcarn once and for all. [PARAGRAPH]With their god vanquished, the followers of The Hand fell to an all time low. They were slow to adapt to a changing world, and reviled by more powerful nations who had been their subjects. The few who maintained the faith however were more fanatical than ever. They realized that the true object of worship was not the person of the god, but his precept. His precept remains, and possessed a powerful will to regain an avatar. It has chosen Auric Ulvin, an orphan from a small outlying Illian village called Brigdarrow, to lead it. He is the greatest magical prodigy born in the current age, and was a very good natured child before the precept claimed him. Driven mad with power, he may end up more evil than Mulcarn ever was by the time he completes his goal and ascends into godhood. [PARAGRAPH:1]This state religion is a prerequisite of [LINK=PROJECT_THE_DEEPENING]The Deepening[\LINK], [LINK=PROJECT_THE_DRAW]The Draw[\LINK], and the [LINK=PROJECT_ASCENSION]Ascension[\LINK] rituals.
[PARAGRAPH:3]Priests and Demons of [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\LINK] will have their ardas most strengthened by the influence of [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\LINK], but also strengthened to a lesser degree by the [LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]The Runes of Kilmorph[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]The Stewards of Inequity[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_ANOINTED]The Anointed[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Between[\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]The Sons of Discord[\LINK]. Its arda will be weakened by [LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]The Children of The One[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]The Matronae[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_EMBER_LEGION]The Ember Legion[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_UNBLEMISHED]The Unblemished[\LINK], the Felllowship of the Leaves, [LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]The Grey Council[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]The Brotherhood of Wardens[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]The Ringgivers[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]Cult of the Dragon[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Order[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]The House of Plenty[\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_FOXMEN]The Foxmen[\LINK]. It will be weakened in Good lands and strengthened in Evil lands. It will be strengthened by proximity to [LINK=BONUS_MANA_ICE]Ice Mana[\LINK], Letum Frigus, the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WHISPERING_WOOD]Whispering Wood[\LINK], [LINK=FEATURE_BLIZZARD]Blizzards[\LINK], [LINK=FEATURE_ICE]Sea Ice[\LINK], [LINK=TERRAIN_SNOW]Ice[\LINK], [LINK=TERRAIN_GLACIER]Glacier[\LINK], [LINK=TERRAIN_WASTELAND]Wasteland[\LINK], or [LINK=TERRAIN_TUNDRA]Tundra[\LINK] terrain. It is weakened by [LINK=BONUS_MANA_FIRE]Fire Mana[\LINK], [LINK=BONUS_MANA_NATURE]Nature Mana[\LINK], [LINK=TERRAIN_DESERT]Desert[\LINK], or [LINK=TERRAIN_BURNING_SANDS]Burning Sands[\LINK] terrain.

[TAB]Forgotten and ignored by the gods, some mortals have turned to worshiping the great dragons who once fought over the land and now lie dormant beneath it. They do not form any unified faith, but are a collection of many conflicting minor cults devoted to different beasts. All agree that the gods' weapons of mass destruction are themselves divine, and find their draconic deities to be much more acceptable than empty prayers offered in temples. All seek to awaken these weapons of mass destruction and see them wreak havoc on their enemies. [PARAGRAPH]These cults can pop up in any land, but are most accepted among the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_KURIOTATES]Kuriotates[\LINK] and [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\LINK]. Those civilizations can complete the [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\LINK] ritual in any city, spreading the Cult to that city, rather than only completing it in a city where the faith is already present. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Cult of the Dragon is unlike other religions. It is not founded by being the first to research a technology. It typically begins when the barbarians create [LINK=UNIT_ACHERON]Acheron's [\LINK] [LINK=BUILDING_WYRMHOLD]Wyrmhold[\LINK] in one of their cities and calls the great Furnace Dragon into the world. It can also be founded by the Kuriotates world spell [LINK=SPELL_LEGENDS]Legends[\LINK], which moves the holy city to the site where it was cast and spreads the religion and the caster's culture to random cities, or by the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_KURIOTATES]Kuriotates[\LINK] or [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\LINK]completing [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\LINK].[PARAGRAPH]The Dragon Cult has numerous disadvantages for most civilizations, although these do not apply to the Kuriotates, the Sheaim, or anyone whose team controls a Dragon. It makes an empire harder to manage and control. Cities that are home to a Dragon Cult are likely to revolt. Anyone with the Fanaticism technology can train a [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC]Dragon Fanatic[\LINK] in a Cult city and use it to spread negative effects to rival cities. These Fanatics can be transformed into devotees of specific dragons when they visit their Wyrmholds or hear them [LINK=SPELL_ROAR]Roar[\LINK]. A standard Fanatic will follow any dragon, but once devoted to a specific beast it will ignore the calls of other dragon species. Dragons generated by Wyrmholds start as sedentary lair guardians, but a Fanatic can use the [LINK=SPELL_BESEECH_DRAGON]Beseech Dragon[\LINK] ability to call the beasts forth from their lairs and try to convince them to attack their enemies. There is a chance that a Dragon will spawn under your control, if you have the right mana, alignment, and follow the Cult of the Dragon as your State Religion. You cannot adopt this as your State religion unless you already have a Dragon.

[TAB]the Laeran Cord thrived throughout the Age of Magic, when the knowledge they curated was prized. These priests of Oghma were welcome in most realms, for they shared their lore freely with all who yearned to learn and stayed as neutral as the god they served. [PARAGRAPH:1]The Age of Ice spelled their ruin. Oghma ignored their prayers to save them. Embarr might have helped, but Ceridwen slayed and tore the archangel asunder, scattering his mind, flesh, and spirit across creation. [PARAGRAPH:1]All original research ceased as the order desperately labored to protect what humanity would need to know to rebuild civilization. The mages among in their ranks were not enough to save them as they fled back to ever fewer hidden libraries. The savage Doviello delighted in their demise, burning both books and men whenever found. [PARAGRAPH:1]In time their hunting parties stopped returning. Some priests went mad. Others died of starvation, or old age. the Laeran Cord dwindled to a single man: a scholar with nothing but a frozen world to study, a teacher without anyone to teach, a high priest only by default. His true name is forgotten. We know him now simply as "Akharien," which means "the last one" in the ancient tongue. [PARAGRAPH:1]In time, the Doviello came for him. Still a young man, born well into the Age of Ice, he knew nothing of world outside what he read in the last library's books. They offered a chance to flee, to survive as a wolf in the wilderness, to one day win the right to join the pack and hunt with them. [PARAGRAPH:1]Instead he threw himself on the books. He begged them to burn him but only spare the library. He promised to tell them all the stories contained within, and to teach them all about the medicinal uses of the few herb that survived in the region. [PARAGRAPH:1]They rejected his offer, believing as they did that the strong need no such knowledge and that the weak it helps preserve deserve to die. This last priest of the Laeran Cord was burned to death within his library. [PARAGRAPH:1]His spirit never passed to Oghma's vault. It lingered to haunt the ruins, fluttering among the dust and ashes which once were books. His ghost had more power than he ever did in life. It scared the Doviello away, but blessed other Vagrants with dreams of distant times and places to inspire them. [PARAGRAPH:1]A new Laeran Cord was refounded early in the Age of Rebirth. The new priests discovered the meager ruins of The Last One's library, but nothing of value remained within except the High Priest's Crown. This was taken to the new church that it might serve Oghma again. It is rumored that the spirit of Akharien followed, and continues to guide the order in relearning what was forgotten. [PARAGRAPH]There is a heresy that emerged within the Cord, rejecting the benevolent guidance of Akharien and wishing to risk experiments with darker forms of magic. Gaelan was a talented summoner and mage in the Laeran Cord. Frustrated with the slow progress within the Cord, Gaelan started the Circle of Gaelan. The Circle gained a reputation for dangerous acts followed by tragedy. While they still believed they were serving Oghma, the new faith in fact followed Ceridwen. There were escaped summoned creatures, death of livestock, a fire that nearly destroyed a village and human experimentation. The worst mistake of the Circle of Gaelan was an attempt to summon a True Angel of Prophecy. They managed to summon A Root of Fear, an Aspect of Mammon whose power had been changed from true Foresight to Foreboding of horrors that become self-fulfilling prophecies. Their greatest fear came true, and the confinement circle failed. The Root of Fear killed all the members except Gaelan himself, drowning them in fears until there was nothing left of them. The vision destroyed Gaelan's body and mind. His past was forgotten, his body horribly disfigured. The battle spread to Euphoria, the Dreamworld where Gaelan's Mind Palace was shattered by Caer lest it fall to Fear. This spread nightmares across Creation. Gaelan himself was reborn as a priest of the Undertow, known only as the Burnt Priest. [PARAGRAPH:2]State religion allows access to:[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_GAELAN]Gaelan Sedracious[\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_LAERAN]Hierophants [\LINK] (unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_ARCHIVE]Archives [\LINK] (building)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]Halves the production cost of: [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_MAGE_GUILD]Mage Guilds[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_LIBRARY]Libraries[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_ACADEMY]Academies[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_GREAT_LIBRARY]The Library of Oghma[\LINK][PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_CROWN_OF_AKHARIEN]The Crown of Akharien[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PALACE_AMURITES]The Amurite Palace[\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:2]Units of this faith are more likely to gain affinity for [LINK=BONUS_MANA_METAMAGIC]Metamagic[\LINK] mana
[PARAGRAPH:3]Priests and Angels of [LINK=RELIGION_LAERAN_CORD]The Laeran Cord[\LINK] will have their ardas most strengthened by the influence of [LINK=RELIGION_LAERAN_CORD]The Laeran Cord[\LINK], but also strengthened to a lesser degree by [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]The House of Plenty[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]The Ringgivers[\LINK], and Eternal Cabal. Its arda will be weakened by [LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]The Children of The One[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]The Matronae[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]The Grey Council[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]The Sons of Discord[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]Cult of the Dragon[\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Between[\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]The Stewards of Inequity[\LINK]. It will be strengthened in Neutral lands and slightly weakened in Good or Evil lands. It will be strengthened by proximity to [LINK=BONUS_MANA_METAMAGIC]Meta Magic Mana[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CAVE_OF_ANCESTORS]the Cave of the Ancestors[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_REMNANTS_OF_PATRIA]the Remnants of Patria[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_RUINS]Ruins[\LINK], or [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITY_RUINS]City Ruins[\LINK]. It is weakened by Mind Mana[\LINK].

As the faith of the Matronae spreads, and other religions loose influence on the world, the ability of the old gods to act in Erebus wanes. If the Matronae faith reaches 100% of the world population, divine magic will die and all priests will be useless. [PARAGRAPH:2]History:[PARAGRAPH]At the end of the Age of Rebirth the demon plagued lands of the Fane of Lessers were conquered and the Throne of Hell destroyed. Not content to just cleanse creation, the archangel Basium lead his angelic army into hell to continue his war. Decades passed and in that time the Bannor used the Crucible to weaken the world's magic. Powerful artifacts of past ages became dusty relics, and those with the talent to be mages in prior ages were rarely able to manifest their power. The Age of Invention had started. [PARAGRAPH]During this age three new goddesses appeared on creation, they were known as the Matronae. Morrigan was the goddess of fate and a great white temple was built to her on the cliffs of the Elohim city of Niveus. From Niveus came the gas Effluvium, which powered city lamp posts and caused divine visions (and would also be used by the Kuriotates to build airships). Sarabride was the goddess of vengeance and her temple was a great foundry built in the reclaimed city of Braduk the Burning. From her city came all sorts of wonders including coal powered trains. The citizens of Braduk built rail systems to connect the major cities of men. The last was Cliodna, the goddess of dreams, and her temple was built on the docks of the Bay of Laurus. From her temple came great steam powered ships that opened up travel to the distant shores of creation. [PARAGRAPH]All three goddesses were active in creation and their religions grew quickly. The religions of ages past, of distant gods who might answer occasional prayers were forgotten, or destroyed by the followers of the Matronae. What use is myth when gods walk among us?[PARAGRAPH:2]The Matronae are the guises assumed by the archangels Gyra, Condatis, and Brigit, who acquired three Masks of the Coven of the Black Candle and used them to steal three Gems of Creation from their respective gods' vaults. They are not interested in becoming gods, or receiving worship. They cannot become avatars that embody their dominions. The compact does not bind them, so they don't need worshipers to permit their actions in any region. They cannot have priests with divine powers, since they don't control a dominion, don't have a fleet of angels to bless their followers, etc. But they are all archangels of fallen gods and they are worried about their dominions becoming corrupted. There is little they can do about it directly, though wars are beginning to start over it. Arak and the Gossamer Legion are coming for Morrigan. After the attack on hell, madness begins spreading through Lanun and Elohim lands as Hastur moves against Cliodna. And the battle between the Swanmay and Sarabride is a prelude to waking up Bhall. [PARAGRAPH]The goal of the Matronae is a lesson from Cassiel. They want to kill worship of the old gods so that the compact keeps them from being able to act in creation. But where Cassiel preached about how the old gods were unworthy, the Matronae have replaced those religions with new fake ones. If they can wipe out the old religions, the gods won't be able to impact creation and damage done by corrupted dominions will be mitigated. They are also reducing the ability of all the gods by claiming the gems. The gods no longer have infinite wells to draw from in three of the six materials. This doesn't mean they aren't powerful, but if the Godswar restarted the gods would be much weaker without the gems. [PARAGRAPH]The Matronae are working closely together. Sarabride and Cliodna are not opposed despite the fact that they are archangels from opposed dominions. They certainly don't agree on everything, but they are working toward the same plan. They rescued Basium from Hell with the hope that he could recover the Font of Life (and Gyra makes a habit of rescuing her idealistic brother), though Basium is nearly destroyed and the Font is guarded by an active god, and they don't currently have another mask (which wouldn't be absolutely necessary, but would certainly help). [PARAGRAPH:2]The Matronae wear Masks of the Coven of the Black Candle for a number of reasons. Protecting their identity is a big one, though in time powers will assume or know who they are. The more they can minimize this the better. Powerful sorcerers can summon and bind archangels (although the Crucible makes this difficult, if not impossible), so the Matronae do not want anyone knowing who they are. They also want to diminish any belief in the old religions, not support it by having people know they are a part of it. Most importantly the masks prevent detection. Anyone hunting, scrying, summoning them won't be able to find them with the masks on. In time, however, the truth will come out. [PARAGRAPH]It is not common knowledge that the Opalus Mortis, Corundum Ardens, and Beryllus Abyssi have been stolen in the first place. Other gods (much less mortals) cannot see into the vaults where Arawn, Bhall, and Danalin once kept them. The gods only knew that a new religion had started centered around some very powerful figures. The evil gods could however deduce the source of their powers and guess at their identities from what happened during their attack on hell. Arak (who has been fighting Gyra for centuries since she killed his wife) and Laroth are also onto Morrigan. [PARAGRAPH:3]All priests have their Ardas weakened by the presence of the Matronae in the world, especially in cities nearby. Once the Matronae influence is strong enough, priests in the vicinity of Apostates will abdondon their leaders and become Apostates themselves

The Compact permits each of the Twenty-One to wield a degree of power over each mortal soul based on the degree that the soul is attached to that god's precept. In order to protect oneself from the malice of one fickle deity, it is common for a man to devote himself fully to that god's enemy. This is dangerous game to play, as leaves one a slave to an equally fallible power. To enjoy true freedom, it is necessary to find the golden mean and practice the virtues found halfway between two vices.

Aristocrats in many lands say "Noblesse oblige. " They believe they must at least appear virtuous, in order to inspire hope and loyalty among the commoners. The Calabim deride such delusions. The Grand Broods know that the victims of the worst abuse are often the most loyal. With methods both magic and mundane, the Brood Guards turn broken souls into fanatics. Calabim thralls fear nothing more than their masters, and would more gladly slit their own throats or wrestle a dragon than risk a Vampire's slightest displeasure. Some learn to enjoy submission. Many tolerate it for the chances it offers to dominate others. A few cling to ambitions of rising in the ranks, perhaps even to becoming a Vampire Lord. Some believe that existence is nothing but suffering, that the heavens are no better than the hells, and that the only escape for an immortal soul is the nirvana of a vampire's kiss. Others believe there is no such thing as a spirit, but that a consciousness can endure indefinitely if it is consumed by and merges with the mind of a Vampire. Most have toyed with several excuses in the past but have ceased trying to rationalize their attachment to the status quo. After a lifetime learning helplessness, they lack the strength of will necessary to imagine things getting better, even if they also cannot fathom them being any worse. The Broods do not care what tales the human cattle tell themselves, so long as they follow orders without question and are quick to present themselves as snacks.

[TAB]Baptism is common to many religions but the Undertow's Cultists hold the victim underwater past immersion, through the struggle, and until the floating body has become filled and heavy with the sacred waters. Then they let go and the corpse rises as the undead Drown.[PARAGRAPH:1]This ability upgrades a Warrior into the Drown. It can only be used if the players state religion is Undertow and if the warrior is in a city with a Temple of the Undertow building or on the same tile as a Cultist.

[TAB]The Undertow priestess stood quietly on the seashore, her long flowing robe dancing in the storm. She could have done this anywhere on land, but nowhere did it feel as real and invigorating as by the sea, by the storm.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Oh mighty masters, hear my call", she spread out her arms and raised her eyes upwards, towards the storm rising above the sea. "My body and mind are yours to command, my sanity but a tool at your bidding. Honor my sacrifice to you, and grant me the sight of your servant." Intoning the words, she could feel the might that lurked deep below the waves, the ancient and inhuman power. The overwhelming sensation was enough to blind her to the living world and threw her mind into a deep blackness that contained only the ever-stormy nightmares of the Undertow. In the horrible, chaotic maelstrom of bizarre sensations and feelings never meant for mortal eyes, she forced her will, shaped in her head the image of a twisted, many-eyed octopus. As she concentrated on the vision, two of the fish's eyes were torn out of its head in a slimly plop. They stared at the chaos around them and floated in the air, untouched by the raging water and wind.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Your eyes shall be mine", she said in a dry whisper, reached out for the eyes and closed her fist around them. As she felt the large, slimy things against her skin, the storm in her mind quieted and she once again stood on the shore.[PARAGRAPH:2]"And my eyes they will be", she finished, now seeing with two pairs of eyes as she opened her fists to reveal the gifts of her gods. She said nothing more as she lowered her hands and willed the eyes to rise up in the air, go out and spy upon the enemies of the Undertow.

[TAB]"My lady... the results of your experiment. Nearly all of them... twisted beyond comprehension..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Those who weren't cut out for this shouldn't have volunteered," the voice of the priestess was as harsh and merciless as the young man's was quivering. "The ones who perish here wouldn't have survived combat anyway."[PARAGRAPH:1]The men and the women who'd volunteered lay prone on the open field, all covered by monstrous deformities. One seemed to have had all the blood sucked out of him, another man's testicles had grown so huge they had crushed his toes under their weight. The priestess was walking among them, inspecting each before moving on. Clearly, it seemed, one of the ones who wasn't cut out for it was the aide she'd been assigned.[PARAGRAPH:1]"But my lady," he tried one more time, flinching away his gaze from the man whose bowels had exploded rather violently out of his stomach, "There wasn't anything wrong with these troops, that's why you chose them... they would have made excellent soldiers had not..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"And you would make an excellent Drown if you did not shut up," the priestess replied coldly, finally quieting the aide. She stopped in front of one of her test subjects, pausing to take a closer look. The elven woman had been pretty once, but no stretch of the imagination would let you use that word of her anymore. Any fat she might have had was muscle now, and all the muscle she had was grown large enough to stretch and tear away the skin that had once covered it. Her eyes were bulging out of her head, the expanding tissue having forced them out of their sockets-but despite everything, she eyed the priestess with an air of wary satisfaction.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I think this... is exactly what we need," for the first time today, a smile slowly appeared on the priestess's lips. Her eyes glowing, she turned to the aide, joyous laughter in her voice. "I knew the Undertow would not forsake us! They have gifted some of us inhuman strength, enough to take down all of our foes. Find the others who look like this, they're the ones we want."[PARAGRAPH:1]"And... the others?" the man slowly asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]"The others? Oh," the priestess shrugged, having entirely forgotten about the failures already, "I don't think they can be made into Drown anymore, can they? It really doesn't matter, do what you want with them." She turned away from the aide, smiling and looking at the elven woman with love and adoration in her eyes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You are so pretty that way, my dear. I'm so glad you made it."

[TAB]The Kraken's swimming was slow, leisurely. Thoughts took a while to cross from one edge of its immense brain to the other, the movements of its tentacles almost independent of its mind. Somewhere, far away on the surface, it could faintly sense a distant call which it couldn't resist. But it was not yet in any rush, instinctively knowing that the caller would need time to prepare.[PARAGRAPH:1]In a lazy motion, one of its tentacles made a slow wave around it, dozens of the small fish surrounding it getting caught in the suction cups. It brought the tentacle back to one of its mouths, dined on its snack. A huge swarm of fish followed it wherever it went-countless of them would end up as its meal, but even more would get to dine on its bigger catches. The swarm stretched back for tens of miles, twice as far as the Kraken itself.[PARAGRAPH:1]Gradually it started getting closer to the surface, could feel the call growing more and more demanding. The fish dispersed in fright and then reassembled as the Kraken began swimming faster, faster than it usually ever did. The alien presence was now a burning sun buried in its brain, no longer willing to tolerate any delay. For all of its size, dwarfing small islands, the Kraken was only a servant for the true lords of the sea.[PARAGRAPH:1]When the chosen of the Undertow called, it would obey and serve with all its might.

The Peliguard is a massive temple that is continuously being constructed by a race of powerful golems. They pay little attention to any of the petitioners, angels or even Nantosuelta herself unless anyone attempts to stop their work or damage the temple. In which case they react violently.[PARAGRAPH]The temple itself is an academy and arena in one. This is the place where angelic champions are trained and prepared for war. Most of this time is devoted to combat, but magic, siegecraft, armorsmithing, weaponsmithing, military strategy, history and mental, physical and spiritual endurance are also trained along with a wide variety of other subjects. Anything that helps prepare them to battle the forces of hell.[PARAGRAPH]This is one of the few vaults where angels of other dominions travel freely. Angels of the other good and neutral gods can often be found here training, or teaching.[PARAGRAPH]There are various, elaborate training programs. But the most intense is known as the Suffering. The Suffering is an assault on the body, mind and spirit of those going through it. Nantosuelta herself watches over the trial. And those that fail often do so by falling and becoming demons. If so Nantosuelta destroys them. Those that survive become paragons of faith. It has been said that no one that survives the Suffering will ever fall. And so far, that has been true. To these few are given the most sensitive of tasks, to bear an artifact that cannot be lost, to travel into the hells or to serve one that cannot be betrayed.

Brujah - 狂暴吸血鬼[NEWLINE][NEWLINE] 吸血鬼不会厌恶自己的残忍天性，大部分吸血鬼喜欢通过有节制的虐待来发泄自己的野性。狂暴吸血鬼却不是这样。经历长期的战乱后，那些在[COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]冰河时代[COLOR_REVERT]中被卡拉比姆公国用作生存依靠的脆弱文明早已纷纷崩溃。甚至在这种吸血鬼领主仅满足于稀少食物的困难时期，狂暴吸血鬼仍陶醉于战斗的虐杀，甚至甘冒毁灭自己不朽生命的风险。当然，他们的结局是无庸置疑的。

Like normal Berserkers, Brujahs cause collateral damage to four other units when attacking stacks. They also start with the vampire promotion and the abilities that come with it, and their Rage ability grants Burning Blood and Enraged to other units nearby instead of only the caster. .

A powerful attacking unit that causes collateral damage to units in the opponent's stack. Their defense is low, so they are most effective when teamed up with high defense units like archers to protect from enemy retaliation. Berserkers can use the Berserk ability, which grants them the Burning Blood and Rage promotions.

Doviello Berserkers carry crude weapons into battle, a throwing rock bigger than a man's head or a stout branch. They use these makeshift weapons because they are temporary. The first opponent killed became the weapon of choice. Grabbed by the ankles they would be swung like a meaty flail. Blood sprayed over opponents and every swing would lose more and more of the corpse until another was needed to replace the first. At this point in the battle the "weapons" were always readily available. Occasionally an opponent would be grabbed while still alive. The effect of being beaten by a bloody body that was screaming at you while it happened is traumatizing to even the most hardened warrior. Few armies were willing to face them. -from "Pack of Wolves" by Dentaro

[TAB]The Gentle One. The Guardian of the Placid Sea. The Scarecrow of the Coward God. The Neutered-Guard-Dog of the Deep. These are translations of some of the more respectful titles recorded in the Dabrei Tanninim (a hundred scroll chronicle of the Godswar composed three decades before Kylorin's birth, known only from commentaries recovered from the Library fo Barathrum) to refer to a beast whose true name had already been forgotten. [PARAGRAPH:2]While gods and dragons warred across Creation, this creature lay safe at the feet of Danalin, below his throne, guarding against threats to Maenalus that never came. He had been made as a sign (an empty threat, some claimed) that Danalin would defend his beloved Aifons if their armies were ever to encroach upon his sacred waters The Great Scaled Dragon was one of many beasts made for this purpose, but his presence was more imposing than all the rest of his lord's horde. [PARAGRAPH:2]Danalin and Sucellus were not dragged into the Godswar until it neared an end; their armies of beasts, angels, and elementals saw little action. The Great Scaled Dragon fought only 4 days in the war before the great truce. He never turned the tide of a single battle in that age, and rarely dared to lead any assault in person. His greatest claim to fame was that he was the first beast to retreat for the meeting at the Seven Pines, and was the first to leave Erebus after the signing of the Compact. The Aifons once sang praises of his prudence. Men and Elves mocked the monster's cowardice. In Kylorin's early armies, "Scaled Dragon" became the byword for a paper tiger. That would change. [PARAGRAPH:2]Incomprehensible omens, visions, dreams of torment too horrid to describe, and prophecies that left the seers catatonic became almost commonplace during the Patrian Civil War. Many signs pointed to a catastrophe looming over the Aifons, and some even named the date of their demise, but no one knew that threat they faced. Kylorin's former pupil, the Aifon Trenton Majosi, traveled all the lands of Erebus seeking salvation for his people, but found none. The closest he came was uncovering a ritual he was told could summon his god into Erebus itself, to personally protect them from whatever doom awaited them. [PARAGRAPH:2]Midway through performing the ritual, perhaps mesmerized by the pendulum swing of his spear, his mind began to wander, pondering the fate of the friends he had made on his quest. Tears welled up within him. As his chants approached the final stanza, he choked up and fell to his knees, unable to continue. He had realized that his actions would unleash a second Godswar on Creation, putting far more lives in peril than he had hoped to save. [PARAGRAPH:2]His family urged him on, but they knew nothing of the hardships other nations had endured why Danalin protected their ancestors alone. His people had had their golden age, but Majosi knew that Man had been denied theirs by the act of pettier gods. He knew they deserved life more than he did. He said as much, but his apprentice would not listen. The boy grabbed the text and tried to pry the sacred spear from his webbed hands to finish the work, but Majosi hurled it into the depths where it remains unto this day. [PARAGRAPH:2]Trenton prayed that his god let them go that he might learn to care for Humanity as he had the Aifons, but the god was not ready to do so. Unable to personally intervene, Danalin unleashed all his beasts into Creation to guard his children, against he knew not what. Leviathan and the Great Scaled Dragon guarded the Isle from each side, awaiting the morning of the Aifon's predicted demise. [PARAGRAPH:2]No man nor god knows what happened on that morn. No Aifon soul reaches Danalin's vault, Arawn's Netherworld, or any heaven or hell. They simply vanished, or were consumed by something too horrible for words. Of the creatures sent to guard them, only Leviathan and the Scaled Dragon remained, but they were never the same. Driven mad by whatever they saw, these once wise and gentle beasts became the most vicious creatures in Creation. Leviathan was confined to the waves, but the dragon roamed far and wide, leveling cities in his wake. The Fire Rain did not slow him, nor did Mulcarn's entry into Erebus once the Illians found and completed Trenton's ritualn. Some claim that not even the new God of Erebus dared to face him, after seeing him devour the Aquilans he had sent to recruit the beast. [PARAGRAPH:2]His rampage could not last forever. In the twenty-third year since the deep freeze, the Beast met his match in Lucar and his horde. Legends tell of six thousand men of valor who saved the world from this abomination, in a sadly Pyrrhic victory. Lucar's spear struck true, but as the dragon breathed it last its heart burst open with not blood, but the greatest flood of brine ever seen in any land. The army arrayed against him was washed away in the deluge, which rushed down into the valley below, eroding twenty mountains, toppling the last of the Thraxian citadels, and drowning all who lived within. When the waters subsided all signs of civilization had been washed to floor bottom of the Aegean, a sea which is said to have tripled in size on that day. [PARAGRAPH:3]With the resurrection of Acheron, Drifa, and Abashi, rumors spread that this beast too may live again. Some Cultists claim that the Lords of the Aegean demand he be given new life, to drown all the realms of men and make all of Erebus submit to the Masters of the Depths. Mumbling Dreamers have begun to shout "Thalatth!" One Speaker of the Tide has proclaimed this to be the true name of the Crazed Dragon, but none can say for sure.

Adventurers are fearless and versatile heroes, which can upgrade to almost any type of unit. True to their name, they love looking for adventure rather than just doing the jobs they are assigned. Adventurers left in the wilderness may find lairs you never knew existed, and explore them without bothering to ask permission first. They will serve dutifully while fighting in hostile territory, but when left to guard the cities of their homeland they tend to get board and abandon their posts. Although it can be annoying at times, their short attention span can serve you greatly. They keep their old skills even after upgrading to something completely different, thus allowing possibilities like knights that can subdue beasts and summon elementals.

The Aquilan are the Seven Aspects of Mulcarn, powerful True Angels who take the form of great eagles that dwell in the heart of blizzards. Many assume that the aquilan seek out the blizzards, but in truth the blizzards are formed wherever the aquilan are.

Men-at-Arms are the upgrades of Axemen and Swordsmen. Their main role remains the same, primarily conquest of enemy cities. They can upgrade into any of three or four quite different units, so consider your goal when choosing promotions for them.

Great Commanders can be used to either recruit units, build a Command Post in a city, or be added to another unit to increase its strength and the rate it gains experience points from combat. The recruit ability offers a quick random assortment of units, but the Command Post tends to have a better long term effect as it adds Great Commander points to the city making getting another all the more likely. A commander that is joined with a unit can always be split from the unit later on and used for other purposes, or joined to a different unit. Commanders may be used instead of Prophets to construct the holy shrines of The Order, The White Hand, and the Cult of the Dragon.

The teachings of Sirona would never permit the Elohim to exalt or exploit Anger, Rage, and Hatred as the armies of most nations do; using Berserkers goes against everything the Elohim stand for. Instead, they employ Counselors who study anger only in order to help others understand the root causes of their suffering and overcome them. As disciples of Sirona they refuse to harm a living soul, but will defend those in their charge. When demons of anger and wrath roam Erebus, thousands remain sane only thanks to these Counselors.

The Elohim Berserker UU serves a very different purpose than most. These defensive-only units can make powerful defenders thanks to their Spirit [LINK=CONCEPT_AFFINITY]affinity[\LINK], and have all levels of the spirit sphere promotions. They are most useful at calming units driven mad with the arrival of the Avatar of Wrath.

This special Undertow unit is created from the Drown spell. Whatever mortal is transformed into a Drown keeps its old base strength plus 2 Death Damage. Being undead, it is immune to death and poison damage. More importantly, Drowns gain the ability to move in coastal tiles as easily as on land, and can move through the Oceans too once the Theology tech is known.

Pixies are the least combat oriented summon. They can defend but not attack. They are more useful to help your workers finish improvements or to sacrifice them in cities to hurry production, gain research, or add culture.

Pixies were created by Amathaon to tend to his gardens. Since Amathaon has retreated from creation they have been left behind and have spread out to any place that features beautiful flowers. Pixies have some magical powers but they mostly relate to simple illusions or the health of plants. They tend to distrust humans except for small children, who they sometimes protect or play with. One or two pixies sometimes abandon their gardens and move into more populated areas, preferring to live in the homes of artists or inventors. They are fascinated by new creations and are known to help with designs and projects when the artist is away or sleeping.

For here, apart, dwells one whose hands have wrought[NEWLINE]Strange eidola that chill the world with fear;[NEWLINE]Whose graven runes in tomes of dread have taught[NEWLINE]What things beyond the star-gulfs lurk and leer. [NEWLINE]Dark Lord of Averoigne-whose windows stare[NEWLINE]On pits of dream no other gaze could bear!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Eidola serve no master but willingly enlist in any deadly conflict. Good religions shun these demonic creatures, or seek them out for destruction, but those who tolerate their vile presence find them to be fearless, deadly warriors, nearly unmatched on any battlefield. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Only evil players can build Eidola.

Eidola are demon disciple units that offer alternate upgrades for Champions and Priests. They require Iron or Mithril and an evil alignment, but no specific building. Priest upgraded to Eidola keep their spells, and melee upgraded to Eidola keep any melee-only promotions they have acquired, so consider upgrading rather than building directly. In any case, they're multi-use units with high strength and free march promotion.

The High Priests of the Empyrean, the Luminaries, have all the abilities of Vicars as well as being able to use the [LINK=literal]Crown of Brilliance[\LINK] spell. The crown does damage to all surrounding enemies and allows the caster to see invisible units.

The Illian Immortals have been given the same blessing and curse as the late Archangel of Ice, Taranis, in order to fill the role of the late archangel under the reign of the new God of Ice. Upon their ascension it becomes impossible to injure them, but equally impossible for them to grow, learn, or adapt to changing situations.

Iron Golems are likely to form the bulk of a Luchuirp army. They have high strength but as golems will not gain promotions from combat. They aren't going to end up as powerful as a highly promoted Man-at-Arms, but losing any one particular iron golem isn't likely to be a huge setback.

Lightbringers have all the abilities of ordinary [LINK=UNIT_DISCIPLE_EMPYREAN]Ecclesiastics[\LINK] and more. Their [LINK=PROMOTION_PERFECT_SIGHT]Perfect Sight[\LINK] lets them see invisible units. Like more advanced [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]Empyrean[\LINK] units, they can help thwart rival spies. More importantly, they have no building requirement, a lower tech requirement, and double the chance to successfully spread the [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN] the Empyrean[\LINK]. This gives the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MALAKIM]Malakim[\LINK] a significant head start in founding and popularizing that faith.

Sluagh are the souls of mortals who have died by not yet departed the world of Erebus. The gods send angels or demons to claim the spirits of their most devout followers, but most are left to wander the plane until they find passage to Arawn's realm. The draw of The Otherworld is strong, but can be resisted. A sluagh may long haunt an area if it feels a strong sense of duty to remain, but lingering too long is healthy for neither the spirit nor the world. These spirits often fall victim to evil necromancers, who raise them as undead monstrosities bound to follow the necromancer's will instead of its own. Only a few heroic souls have the strength of will to maintain their sanity, sense of identity, and the hope for a true resurrection. Resurrection spells cannot reach beyond the caster's own plane to restore any soul that has already entered its god's vaults. The Elohim obviate this restriction by assigning a soul catcher to their monarchs. A soul catcher is a mage specializing in spirit magic who can trap the soul after death and hold it until a resurrection is available. A god can answer prayers to send souls they have claimed back to Erebus for resurrection, but this is exceedingly rare. The only known examples are Duin Halfmorn and Arthendain, who were sent back by Camulos and Sucellus respectively.

The Luonnotar are the most powerful disciple units to which the Grigori have access. Although they lack the spell abilities of priests and high priests, they are immune to magic, very strong in combat against other disciples, and can target disciple units in stacks with better defenders. They can move through rival territory without open border agreements, evangelizing the Children of The One religion to cities and units alike. Priests who adopt their faith are defrocked-- automatically disbanded. Other converts gain Scourge and Magis Resistance. In cities the faith can cause Monotheist revolts, forcing out other religions. Even state religions can be removed, plunging the city into chaos. The Grigori get a free Luonnotar when they first learn Arcane Lore, and can use it to found the Children of The One.

Monks are great for fighting demonic units. They also have the Medic promotion, making them decent healers. They don't need a building to train so they can be created in any city. They have Spirit [LINK=CONCEPT_AFFINITY]affinity[\LINK], making them extremely powerful if you control eough of that mana. .

Radiant Guards have several advantages over axemen. They can see invisible, they start with the Guardsman promotion (allowing them to protect stacks from assassins and marksmen), and they can cast the Blinding Light spell to hold enemies in place. They can upgrade into Men-at-Arms or Rathas, which have all the strenghs of Chariots and more. They do not require Training Yards but do require both the Empyrean religion and a Fenestran Temple to be present in the city. They normally require the Empyrean state religion too, but the Overcouncil may pass a resolution allowing its members to ignore that restriction.

Rathas have several advantages over chariots. They can see invisible, they can cast the Blinding Light spell to hold enemies in place, and they have an a combat advantage against and the ability to target the sort of units which are enemies of Lugus. They may be trained only by those with the Empyrean as their state religion in cities where that faith and its temples are present.

Rathus Denmora has all the abilities of both [LINK=UNIT_GHOST]Ghosts[\LINK] and [LINK=UNIT_DIVIDED_SOUL]Divided Souls[\LINK], but his true value is as the ultimate counter other [LINK=PROMOTION_HERO]heroes[\LINK]. He specifically targets heroes in stacks of stronger units (except in cities), and starts with the [LINK=EQUIPMENT_NETHER_BLADE]Nether Blade[\LINK]. This otherworldly sword guarantees victory against heroes, and makes its victims ineligible for resurrection until the equipment is destroyed.

The Brood Guard is more expensive than the standard Royal Guard, is not quite as strong a defender, and cannot give Hope to the populace, but as the earliest unit to start with Vampirism they are nonetheless superior. They still require the Aristocracy civic and will abandon you if that civic is changed.

[TAB]The Runewyns are winged angels of Dagda who are immune to all magic. They are frequently sent to battle powerful wizards or to cross magical barriers. They can drain away all but the most powerful spells with a touch.

Stygian Guards require a Temple to the Undertow and Copper to train. They are Immune to Disease, like all Demons, and heal faster than men, as indicated by their March promotion. They can move both on land in in Coastal tiles, and even in the Oceans once Theology is known.

The Trojan Horse can travel in rival territory and carry hidden units in before an attack is announced, or just used to slip through the territory of rivals who refuse to give you an Open Borders agreement (or whom you don't want to allow into your lands). The Trojan Horse is unique.

These wandering souls can be created by that units Astral Projection ability, which requires the [LINK=PROMOTION_DIVINE]Divine[\LINK] promotion and [LINK=PROMOTION_COVEN]The Between[\LINK] religion, or an [LINK=UNIT_EATER_OF_DREAMS]Eater of Dreams[\LINK] in the same stack, or the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SIDAR]Sidar's [\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_DIVIDED_SOUL]Divided Soul[\LINK]. They are invisible and can explore rival territory with impunity, even investigating rival cities. The Astral Body has the Call Form ability, which summons its physical body to its tile and deletes the unit. (This cannot be used when they are already on the same tile.) The Astral Body is deleted when its body is killed. (Due to limitations in the code, it must also be deleted when its summoner upgrades to another unit. )

[TAB]How many roles have I played? They blur together in my mind. [PARAGRAPH:1]I was a victim from the moment my life began. An attacker came for my mother even as she gave birth to me. He possessed Garrus, a simple stable boy and used him to sneak up through the inn to my parents' room. He tried to get close to my mother, to attack her at her most vulnerable. My father fought to stop him. The details are unknown except that a battle occurred in the room and my father was struck a mortal blow. With his last breath he uttered a holy word that destroyed the spirit possessing Garrus and collapsed the entire inn. [PARAGRAPH:1]My mother died in the collapse, my father died from the attack. The stable boy was pulled from the rubble, one arm was crushed but he appeared otherwise healthy. My soul fled the dying infants form and took home in his newly evacuated body. I was born into the body of a teenage boy. [PARAGRAPH:1]The innkeeper raised me, teaching me as if I had simply forgotten my life and in a few years I served him well. He raised me as he rebuilt the inn. But I always knew that Garrus wasn't my name and I listened intently when those that survived the collapse retold the story. [PARAGRAPH:1]We didn't know much about my parents, but my father wore the yellow robes of a priest of the Empyrean. There was a small temple to the god in our city and when I was ready I joined their ranks as a disciple. Within the clergy my identity didn't matter, I was simply a child of Lugus. My superiors praised my empathy, questioned my maturity and laughed when I said that I thought I was the son of a priest. They claimed no such priest had visited the city and considered my thoughts the wishful thoughts of boy with too much imagination. [PARAGRAPH:1]My right arm was still crushed. By this point it was shriveled and permanently wrapped against my side. When I asked if it could be healed the priests prayed over it, but it never got better. Others came and received healing, nobles, merchants, beggars, soldiers, but I remained maimed. [PARAGRAPH:1]One day in early Aedrini the temple was in an uproar. Priests barked orders, disciples scurried about trying to look busy. No one had thought to wake me. After many questions a priest finally gave me my answer. [PARAGRAPH:1]"The Luminary Chalid is coming child, so stay out of the way. "[PARAGRAPH:1]I began to retreat to my chamber when he yelled after me, "And don't bother him when he arrives!"[PARAGRAPH:1]That next day a single man arrived on a dappled grey mare. He rode without an escort and though he needed no guards on the road, he could have used some outside of the temple. He was immediately mobbed by well meaning disciples, genuflecting priests and hordes of gawking townspeople. He wore the robes of a Luminary and I wondered if my father wore the same. [PARAGRAPH:1]He spent the next three days in our hastily constructed council chamber. The chamber was open for anyone to hear the deliberation and speak in an orderly manner. They discussed the towns role in the Overcouncil, local legislation and a problem with brigands in the area. [PARAGRAPH:1]The council meetings always went well into the night, and Chalid attended every dawn ceremony. He only had a few hours between to get some sleep. I was hurrying to the dawn service one morning when I found him standing alone in the refectory looking out the windows toward the east. The morning bell rung, signaling the dawn ceremony was about to start and Chalid turned to find me staring at him. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Morning disciple, are you ready to receive our lords blessing?"[PARAGRAPH:1]I managed to stammer something unintelligible out. Despite that he smiled at me with true affection and clasped me on the shoulder. That was the first he noticed my withered arm. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Do you have something to ask me?" he said. [PARAGRAPH:1]He expected me to ask for healing, but that didn't matter to me. Instead I asked, "What sort of spirit attacked my mother?"[PARAGRAPH:1]He put his arm around me and we walked to the sanctuary together. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Let me pray about it" he said. [PARAGRAPH:1]The service was exactly like all the others but I paid little attention. Instead I watched Chalid. He looked confused as he prayed, sometimes pained, sometimes resigned and I imagined that it had something to do with my question. [PARAGRAPH:1]I waited after the service. Chalid spoke briefly with the vicar who had performed the service and meet a few of the members. Then he left the sanctuary and went into the council chambers. [PARAGRAPH:1]I spent the day neglecting my duties and waiting outside the council chamber. Just past nightfall the towns warning bells rang out; guards ran through the streets yelling that brigands were attacking. [PARAGRAPH:1]Everyone flooded out of the temple. At the edge of the town shapes rushed through the darkness. Black tipped arrows cut guards down where they writhed screaming in pain. Guards brought torches and under the cover of shield men they retook the fortifications while the shadows simply moved to attack at another point. [PARAGRAPH:1]A voice from the darkness called, "What good is a god that abandons you every night?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Chalid ignored the taunt and ordered the men back within the cities lantern light. He alone bounded over the wall and in to the darkness at the cities edge. His mace glowed faintly in the starlight and though we couldn't see any attackers on the open field we all knew they were moving in on him. [PARAGRAPH:1]Chalid prayed and an aura of golden fire burst up around his head and dark men caught fire on the field, on the walls, and even a few that had snuck into the city. The holy fire consumed them and guards rushed in to beat or capture the men. [PARAGRAPH:1]But one was not distracted by the fire. It clung to his black armor and that of his steed but he rode soundlessly towards Chalid, like a shadow of a dark god stretching out to touch him. Chalid raised his mace up, and then back down and the field was lit up as if it was day. A pillar of golden fire, like the sun itself but full of righteous fury, crushed the rider. There was a horrific scream and then when the pillar retreated back up into the sky the rider was gone. [PARAGRAPH:1]I spent the night tending to the guardsmen wounded in the attack. Their wounds festered from poison and the men passed between fevered dreams and anguish when awake. There was little I could do but try to keep their wounds clean and try to make them comfortable. Chalid and the priests prayed over the men and some were healed, but too many were injured. [PARAGRAPH:1]That next morning I returned to my chambers to wash up and change into fresh clothes, as did most of the temple. I headed again to the dawn ceremony and found Chalid alone again in the refectory looking out towards the east. [PARAGRAPH:1]"You saved the town. " It sounded hollow when I said it. Unsuited to the miracle I had witnessed. [PARAGRAPH:1]"I only had faith that Lugus would protect me, he did everything else. "[PARAGRAPH:1]I smiled, the warmth Chalid had shared with me yesterday was gone now. He looked troubled but I assumed it was just the events of the long night. I know he hadn't slept either. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Did you find out anything about my mother?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Chalid looked at the floor, the morning bells rang though neither of us moved. [PARAGRAPH:1]"I should lie to you" Chalid said, "the mandate of truth is sometimes painful. I am sorry. I won't lie but I will warn you, it would be better if you did not know. "[PARAGRAPH:1]"I want to know" I argued with more passion than I intended, "Knowledge, truth, revelation are the precepts of Lugus. I should know my own past. "[PARAGRAPH:1]"The woman's name was Magda de'Vala" Chalid started, "The man wasn't her husband but her guardian, though he was a priest of the Empyrean. The child was prophesied to be a great hero, which is why many sought to kill Magda and her baby. "[PARAGRAPH:1]He paused, but I only waited for him to continue. [PARAGRAPH:1]"The stable boy Garrus died three days before the attack. That which killed Garrus, that which killed Magda's guardian and caused the collapse that killed Magda and her baby. that was you. "[PARAGRAPH:1]I was furious and I rushed out of the refectory. Chalid watched me go then headed into the sanctuary. My thoughts went back to those early days. I never felt like I was the stable boy. And for the first time I questioned my origin. Would a baby's spirit in a boy's body be able to adapt that quickly? Could even a possessed stable boy be able to overcome a priest of Lugus, or was that creature something darker? And was I that creature?[PARAGRAPH:1]I stopped in the temples infirmary. Except for the wounded it was empty, everyone in the temple was in the dawn ceremony despite those laying here near death. There was only one man awake, a bandage covered his left thigh. I knelt at his bedside. When I saw the torment he was in I forgot a bit of my own. [PARAGRAPH:1]"What is your name?" I asked. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Abin," he said, "I'm a jeweler who pretended to be a city guard. "[PARAGRAPH:1]That wasn't unusual. Our city was too small to maintain full time guardsmen so most were volunteers with other jobs. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Either you are too good at pretending, or not good enough. "[PARAGRAPH:1]He gave me a weak smile. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Can I pray for you?" I asked. He nodded. [PARAGRAPH:1]I placed my hand on him and closed my eyes. I have seen many healed but I had never performed a miracle myself. If I could do this, if I could heal this man and channel the power of Lugus then I couldn't be whatever creature Chalid thought I was. Maybe I was the holy child, maybe the attack on Magda de'Vala failed. [PARAGRAPH:1]I could feel his labored breath. I could feel his pain, feel his love for his large family of nieces and nephews. His quiet store and hours spent working on small intricate jewelry. And I felt him die. [PARAGRAPH:1]Then I felt the poison strike, it burnt through my body focused on the wound in my left thigh. I stepped away from the bed in shock. I was taller and my robes, which were big on me, were now tight. And my formerly withered arm was now trapped uncomfortably in its folds. [PARAGRAPH:1]I loosened the robe and held out my full, strong arm. But it didn't look like my arm; it was the jewelers arm. As I looked at myself I realized that I was identical to the dead body of the jeweler that lay in the bed in front of me. And then the poison struck again and sent me to my knees. I picked myself up and fled the temple in pain and confusion. [PARAGRAPH:1]Pain will drive you mad and it only took a few hours of suffering like this before I found a farmer out working in his field. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Blind goats Abin!" he said, "what is wrong with you? Why are you wearing a disciple's robes?"[PARAGRAPH:1]I threw him to the ground and held him, smashing him once in the face when he tried to fight back. I felt for that closeness, I reached out to find everything that he was, and the pain drifted away. When I opened my eyes I saw him staring up at his own reflection in horror. The last I saw him he was running toward his farmhouse, I started running as well. I don't think I have ever stopped. [NEWLINE][PARAGRAPH:1]I still don't know what I am. All the roles that I've played since then blur together in my mind. I've gotten better at reading people and worked for a time for an assassins' guild, simply for reading people I touch. During other times I steal the lives of those I wish to share. I tried the lavish extravagance of princes and wealthy merchants, but there is little to envy them for once you understand how they truly live. The best stolen lives come from the simple fathers of large families, those that have the love and respect of everyone in their lives. Dump the body of one of those in a shallow grave and I have a few good weeks of fun before I become bored and move on to something else. [PARAGRAPH:1]Maybe Chalid was right, maybe I am a monster.

The Empyrean is the youngest major faith in Erebus, having been organized only by its current Patriarch. The worship of the God of Light, however, is truly ancient. There were temples built in what would later become the Desert of Myrh which survived the worst of the Godswar, yet none survived the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH:1]Lanthus was a young Acolyte of Lugus from a time before the kingdoms of Man were first united. He was a righteous boy who lived a peaceful life of service to his community, until the day he met Alexis. In her quest to find immortality, she committed acts against him more egregious than any yet committed by mortal against mortal. She tortured him past the point that a living soul could bare, but would not let him die. When the finally had enough and decided to let is spirit leave his flesh, she devoured it and denied him the eternal rest that his god would have granted. Lugus is a forgiving lord, but even his forgiveness has bounds. He insists on actual repentance, on true contrition. Alexis could not find it in her heart to regret anything, but rejoiced in her inequity and proudly spread the secret of her dark arts to others just as cruel. Where all compassion had failed, Lugus considered it his duty to supplement the conscience, and so he cursed Alexis and her dark progeny. From that day forth, every beam of sunlight to touch a vampire's skin delivers with it a taste of all the suffering inflicted on others. While this causes no physical harm, it induces panic in minds unused to empathy and denies access to the superhuman powers stolen from the souls of others. [PARAGRAPH:1]Lugus always aims for the betterment of those he chastens, but the vampires refused to see his tough love through their own hate. They considered the curse a sign of a vendetta against them, and declared their own vendetta in return. Once Patria fell and could not constrain them, Alexis and Flauros led a campaign to eradicate every soul that honored the God of Truth. His church was destroyed. Every priest was executed. Every holy text was burned. Not one sentence of his doctrine was preserved intact. The Calabim made sure that the church of Lugus could not reemerge for over 600 years. [PARAGRAPH:2]It is however hard to crush the values of the human soul. The Malakim never abandoned their love of truth and openness. From time to time and in many tribes holy men would emerge and espouse such virtues. Lugus himself spoke into the hearts of many of these Lightbrigers. At the start of the Age of Rebirth, the name of Lugus was heard again. When the Once-Elf Varn Gosam wandered into the Desert of Myrh from the Vale of Shadows, he found a faith already emerging. He did not found the Empyrean by converting heathens, but by bringing together those who already loved The Light. Varn had united most of the Malakim in the worship of Lugus before he set out into the deep desert to find the legendary Mirror of Heaven, where Lugus reveled to him his holy doctrines in full.

These demons (also called "Drinkers") consume the souls of their victims, becoming more powerful each time they kill someone. After a few kills the Ira becomes so powerful opponents are better served to hide until they return to normal rather than try to kill it. [LINK=SPELL_ASSUAGE]Calming[\LINK] spells are very effective against Ira, and weaken them considerably.

[TAB]The Luchuirp assaulted the Illian city. Juggernauts slammed against the defenses. Towering iron golems waded through the rubble, destroying any defenders they found. The Luchuirp forces tried to stop the ritual that was taking place within the inner city, but they were too late. [PARAGRAPH:1]When Mulcarn entered the city, entered creation, the battle stopped. A layer of ice spread from the first place his foot touched outwards through the city and across the land. The Luchuirp army was destroyed, dwarves killed, golems frozen. Even the Illian macemen were frozen in place, kept unchanged until Mulcarn needed them. [PARAGRAPH:1]As he surveyed his new dominion he picked up one of the Luchuirp golems. He admired their fortitude. They were unaffected by the cold and their unchanging nature. All traits Mulcarn prized. [PARAGRAPH:1]He whispered a new life into the golem, "Make me more. " [PARAGRAPH:1]"As you command" was Barnaxus's reply.

Illusionists have the abilities of normal mages, and also the abilities granted by the Illusionist promotion. Unlike in base FfH2, this does not make their summons illusions, but instead allows them to create illusionary duplicates of other units nearby. These illusions cannot attack much less kill opponents, but can be quite useful decoys to help defend your real troops.

Liches are Archmages who seek immortality through a sort of suicide. They use Necromancy to bind their own souls within their corpses, saving themselves from the horrors of hell, or any afterlife outside Erebus. The Lich's undead form is sustained through magic. Some use spells to preserve their flesh, some cast glamors to maintain the appearance of life, and some prefer to terrify their enemies by opening flaunting their corruption for all to see. Liches are always powerful casters and can be difficult to vanquish. They are naturally immortal, and restore their immortality with every kill. They are immune to all poisons and death damage, strong against unholy, but are vulnerable to holy damage, Undead Slaying, and the Destroy Undead spells. Each player is allowed only one Lich at a time. They must be upgraded from level 8+ units in a city with a Tower of Necromancy.

Valkyries were created to battle the demons who were stealing souls undeserving of hell. They escort the claimed to the heavens and attack demons attempting to stop the unclaimed from traveling to Arawn's realm.
The Ophanim are flying chariots manned by angels. They are swift and terrible. Though they fly their wheels still spin with the sound of crunching bones.

Heralds have the Herald's Call ability, which grants the Herald's Blessing promotion. This is both a blessing and a curse. It makes living units significantly more powerful, but then usually kills them within a few turns. They can return as Angels once they die, but it is still a good idea not to use this spell around units that are more useful alive than dead.

Angelic messengers often used to convey important messages. They convey not only words but usually powerful blessings, for example Nantosuelta may send a Herald to a general that grants valor and strength to his army. Priestesses of Ceridwen have been known to be able to capture and use the blessing of a Herald to their own ends

Bhall's Archangel Brigit can never be built, only [LINK=SPELL_FREE_BRIGIT]freed[\LINK] from the [LINK=literal]Ring of Carcer[\LINK] by a level 14+ unit once [LINK=literal]Fanaticism[\LINK] is known. If Brigit acquires a [LINK=MASK_OF_ESUS]Mask of Esus[\LINK], she may [LINK=SPELL_RETRIEVE_CORUNDUM_ARDENS]retrieve the Heart of Fire[\LINK] and transform herself into [LINK=UNIT_SARABRIDE]Sarabride, Goddess of Vengeance[\LINK], and found The Matronae.

Arawn's Archangel Gyra can never be built, only rescued from [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_BRADELINES_WELL]Bradeline's Well[\LINK] or summoned using a Mercurian Gate and Death Affinity. If Gyra acquires a [LINK=MASK_OF_ESUS]Mask of Esus[\LINK], she may [LINK=SPELL_RETRIEVE_OPALUM_MORTIS]retrieve the Ending Stone[\LINK] and transform herself into [LINK=UNIT_MORRIGAN]Morrigan, Goddess of Fate[\LINK], and found The Matronae.

Danalin's Archangel Condatis can never be built, only rescued from [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_AIFON_ISLE]Maenalus[\LINK]. If Gyra acquires a [LINK=MASK_OF_ESUS]Mask of Esus[\LINK], she may [LINK=SPELL_RETRIEVE_BERYLLUM_ABYSSI]retrieve the Ocean's Tear[\LINK] and transform herself into [LINK=UNIT_CLIODNA]Cliodna, Goddess of Dreams[\LINK], and found The Matronae.

Aeron's Archangel Odio can never be built, only [LINK=SPELL_FREE_ODIO]freed[\LINK] from [LINK=literal]Odio's Prison[\LINK] by a level 11+ unit once [LINK=literal]Rage[\LINK] is known. Odio and the Ira whom he can summon are vulnerable to the [LINK=literal]Assuage[\LINK] spell.

Ira are special units that may be summoned by the [LINK=UNIT_WRATH]Avatar of Wrath[\LINK] or created in combat by [LINK=literal]Odio[\LINK]. Although they start relatively weak, they go stronger whenever they kill an opponent. They are vulnerable to the [LINK=literal]Assuage[\LINK] spell.

Chaos Marauders may appear in Sheaim cities with [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gates[\LINK] and [LINK=BUILDING_CARNIVAL]Carnivals[\LINK], and may be also summoned by the Chaos II spell. The summoned Marauders start out [LINK=literal]Rebellious[\LINK], difficult to control and likely to betray you to the barbarian state. In either case the unit start out [LINK=literal]Mutated[\LINK] and are vulnerable to the [LINK=SPELL_ASSUAGE]Assuage[\LINK] spell.

Camulos originally created the Pacales as diplomats and traders. These angels were gifted with the ability to speak and understand any language as their original purpose was to smooth out relations between any intelligent species that may have conflict. That plan didn't last long. Shortly after the Angel of Peace fell to become the God of Strife, these peacemakers reversed their roles and became Chaos Marauders. These demons serve as mercenaries for hire, doing anything within their power to cause strife between various individuals, races, and empires. They still retain the ability to understand any language, but their speech jumps randomly between languages, making it nearly impossible for anyone but other marauders to understand more than small bits of what they are saying.

Reborn in the land by unknown means, Duin has been cursed with Lycanthropy: any living unit he slays (except animals, beasts, and those actually just captured) may become a Ravenous Werewolf that will follow him. [PARAGRAPH:1]This unit is the avatar of the leader with the same name. If said leader is alive in the game, it will switch to that player's control. The death of a leader's avatar unit costs the leader his traits; the resurrection of such a unit restores those traits.

Abashi is among the greatest of Ceridwen's [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_OBSIDIAN]Obsidian Serpents[\LINK]. She is not randomly generated from a Wyrmhold lair like her sisters, but may be trained directly by a Sheaim player after the [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\LINK] ritual is completed. Like all [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_OBSIDIAN]Obsidian Serpents[\LINK], her [LINK=SPELL_BREATH_NEXUS]breath weapon[\LINK] is a bean of purple light that most think merely kills its victims, but may actually teleport them to a random location. Her roar transforms [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC]Dragon Fanatics[\LINK] to [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC_OBSIDIAN]Obsidian Serpent Fanatics[\LINK], as does that of her kin, but unlike them she cannot be compelled to attack a Fanatic's enemies via their [LINK=SPELL_BESEECH_DRAGON]Beseech Dragon[\LINK] ability.
